## Overview Adds `tools/vllm-simulator`, the simulator half of RFC #61406. It runs the real vLLM v1 engine on a CPU-only host and bypasses model forward. A simulation clock then advances by a hardware-aware per-step latency prediction. The output is the same set of metrics `vllm bench serve` reports, for a target model, accelerator, and parallel configuration. This PR is fully independent of the CPU-based CI PR (#61407) and modifies no file outside `tools/vllm-simulator`. Once #61407 lands, the simulator can be simplified on top of it: its own mock platform and model-runner stub can be replaced, and real parallel ranks become possible. See [Relationship to the CPU-based CI PR](#relationship-to-the-cpu-based-ci-pr). The simulator is built by the same team, and with the same design, as the SGLang simulator (sgl-project/sglang#21891). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Maintainer decisions needed:** where the simulator should live, and which engine seams it may hook. See [Decisions requested](#decisions-requested). ## Claims - **Transparent to users.** Serving and the local engine API accept the same arguments and expose the same interfaces as `vllm serve`, `vllm bench serve`, and `AsyncLLM`. - **Zero changes to vLLM.** All 56 files are under `tools/vllm-simulator`, of which the core vLLM hooks (`src/vllm_simulator/simulation/vllm`) account for 1428 lines. Request admission, scheduling, prefix caching, block allocation, and KV-connector bookkeeping run on unmodified vLLM code. - **Two clock modes.** `NON_BLOCKING` (default) advances a virtual clock. `BLOCKING` sleeps for the predicted latency, so the server can stand in for a real deployment in real time. - **Pluggable predictors:** [AISimulate](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate) (default), replay table, sklearn model, and linear model. See [Predictors](#predictors). - **Topologies:** multi-instance with load balancing, and PD disaggregation through the native `DecodeBenchConnector`. - **Baseline collector.** Exports per-iteration batch composition and latency from real GPUs, for replay tables, ML predictor training, and accuracy validation. ## Validation **Functional tests.** Run on a CPU-only host with no CUDA runtime, against the [AISimulate](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate) `SOL` database for a simulated B300. Models cover the main attention and KV-cache layouts: - dense GQA: Qwen3-8B; - hybrid full attention + Gated DeltaNet: Qwen3.5-27B; - sparse MLA (DSA): GLM-5; - hybrid MLA + KDA: Kimi-K3; - compressed sparse MLA: DeepSeek-V4-Pro. ```bash cd tools/vllm-simulator && pip install . for t in test/test_simulation_*.py; do python -m pytest "$t" -v -s; done ``` | Test | Coverage | Result | |---|---|---| | `test_prefix_cache_and_offload` | All models above: device prefix-cache hit, CPU-offload hit after eviction, cache flush | PASSED | | `test_vllm_serving_blocking` | OpenAI server, `BLOCKING` | PASSED | | `test_vllm_serving_non_blocking` | OpenAI server, `NON_BLOCKING`, `bench_serving` client | PASSED | | `test_benchmark_round_robin` | 3 engines, round-robin routing | PASSED | | `test_pd_disagg_benchmark` | 1P + 1D, merged TTFT across instances | PASSED | **Large-scale deployment test.** A one-hour workload on the prefill instances of a large-scale PD-disaggregated test deployment was replayed in the simulator: 60 prefill instances, behind cache-aware routing, with an external prefix cache (KV connector to an external KV store) enabled. | Metric (1 h mean) | Simulation | Real | Difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Request rate (RPS) | 168.29 | 168.25 | +0.02% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 478.35 | 518.23 | −7.7% | | Cache hit ratio (%) | 77.25 | 77.86 | −0.61 pp | - **Request rate** matches by construction, because arrivals are replayed from the trace. - **Cache hit ratio** follows the per-minute fluctuations within about 1 pp. - **TTFT** tracks the real trend but stays consistently lower. That is the same direction as the unmodelled engine residual listed under [Limitations](#limitations). ## Details ### Why hooks instead of in-tree changes The primary goal is a workflow that is transparent to users. | Workflow | Real | Simulated | |---|---|---| | Serving | `vllm serve` | `python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server` | | Benchmark | `vllm bench serve` | `python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving` | | Local engine | `AsyncLLM.generate` | same code, after `init_hook()` | Arguments, request formats, and output metrics are unchanged. The entry point can also stay unchanged by installing the hooks from a startup file, either a [`.pth` import line](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#path-extensions-pth-files) or, on Python ≥ 3.15, a [`.start` entry point](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#startup-entry-points-start-files). Such a file would need an environment-variable gate, and this PR does not ship one. An in-tree implementation would spread non-serving changes across `vllm/`: - arrival replay; - a virtual clock; - stats export; - a device-less platform and model runner; - no-op connector transfers. Each of these would add branches to hot paths. Hooks keep all of them in `tools/vllm-simulator`. They are installed at class-definition time, before vLLM is imported. **Maintenance cost.** Keeping the hooks outside `vllm/` does not make them free to maintain. The cost depends on how close each hook sits to low-level code, and the hooks fall into two kinds: - **`wrapped_*` functions** keep the native call and only add simulation state around it: arrival replay, the clock, and stats. They sit on engine-level interfaces (`EngineArgs`, `EngineCore`, `UniProcExecutor`) that rarely change. - **`override_*` functions** replace native behavior, almost entirely to remove hardware dependencies: device initialization, memory profiling, pinned buffers, and transfers. Together with the mock platform and the model-runner stub, these are the hooks most tightly coupled to low-level code. That is exactly the layer meta-CI (#61407) covers in-tree, alongside the code it depends on. Once #61407 lands, these hooks can be removed, leaving only the stable `wrapped_*` interfaces. Hooks also apply to modules outside vLLM. External components, such as KV stores with their own capacity management, can therefore be brought into the simulation directly instead of waiting for each one to add simulation support. ### Design - **Engine core.** `EngineCore.add_request` parks requests until the clock reaches their logical `created_time`. `UniProcExecutor.execute_model` converts each `SchedulerOutput` into `(scheduled tokens, past KV length)` pairs, queries the predictor, and advances the clock. `EngineCore.profile` dumps per-request and per-iteration stats. - **Worker.** A stub stands in for Model Runner V2. The KV-cache spec comes from a meta-device model walk under the simulated TP size and accelerator architecture. The KV budget comes from the target accelerator's HBM. - **Connectors.** KV offload and PD transfers complete immediately, so scheduler-side hits behave normally. ### Predictors Each predictor maps one step's batch, a list of `(scheduled tokens, past KV length)` pairs, to a latency. The predictor is selected by `predictor.name` in the simulator config. | Predictor | Source of latency | Typical use | |---|---|---| | `aisimulate` (default) | [AISimulate](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate) per-operator performance model for the target model, accelerator, and TP/EP size. Database modes: `SILICON` (measured kernels), `HYBRID`, `EMPIRICAL`, `SOL`, `SOL_FULL` (speed-of-light). | Hardware that is not available locally; capacity planning | | `replay` | Real per-iteration latencies exported by the baseline collector, matched by exact batch composition, with optional KNN interpolation on misses | Debugging by separating predictor error from scheduler and cache behavior | | `ml` | sklearn regressor trained on collector exports, over batch-composition features | A deployed model and accelerator with collected baselines | | `linear` | `base_ms + per_token_ms × scheduled tokens`; a constant step latency when `per_token_ms = 0` | Debugging | ### Relationship to the CPU-based CI PR The two efforts are independent by nature. - **Origin of meta-CI.** #61407 grew out of discussions in which functional CI also turned out to need CPU execution. It is in-tree because it goes deeper than the simulator: execution reaches model forward and runs fake kernels through their full lifecycle. - **What the simulator gains.** The simulator never executes model forward. For it, meta-CI only reduces the CPU-execution support it has to carry itself. - **Plan.** #61407 is not merged and may still change, so this PR ships its own minimal mock platform and model-runner stub. Once meta-CI lands, a follow-up will drop the `override_*` hooks, simplify the model runner, and allow real TP/EP/PP ranks. The `wrapped_*` hooks and the out-of-tree approach stay as they are. ### Decisions requested 1. **Location and ownership.** Is `tools/vllm-simulator` acceptable as a separately installed package with its own dependencies? 2. **Hooked seams.** The hooks cover `EngineArgs`, `EngineCore`, `Scheduler`, `UniProcExecutor`, `Worker`, the platform, and three KV-connector workers. Should any of these become narrow public extension points, such as a request-arrival hook or a step-latency callback? ### Limitations - **Version coupling.** A hook that fails to apply logs a warning, so a renamed method can degrade silently. - **Accuracy.** Only the comparison above is reported. `NON_BLOCKING` does not model the ~2.5 ms/step engine residual. - **Scope.** Text generation only, on Model Runner V2, eager mode, synchronous scheduling. Parallelism is modelled by the predictor only. - **KV cache transfer.** Transfer time is not modelled yet, for either external prefix cache loads and stores or PD prefill-to-decode transfers. Both complete instantaneously, so only the hit and miss decisions are simulated. Transfer models are follow-up work. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@
+# vllm_simulator
+## Background
+As large language models (LLMs) are rapidly deployed at scale for inference services, inference performance directly impacts user experience, service cost, and resource efficiency. Key metrics such as Time to First Token (TTFT), Time Per Output Token (TPOT), and system throughput are highly dependent on the complex interplay among model architecture, hardware platforms (e.g., A100/H100/B300), inference engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM), and runtime configurations (e.g., quantization, batching, and parallelism strategies).
+
+Traditional end-to-end stress testing on real GPU clusters is expensive and time-consuming, making it impractical to efficiently explore the vast space of configuration combinations. To address this, we propose **vllm_simulator**, a high-fidelity CPU-based simulation system. vllm_simulator enables fast, low-cost, and high-fidelity prediction of key performance metrics across different models, target hardware, and configurations by replaying real-world inference workload traces collected from production or representative scenarios, thereby accelerating the design and optimization of inference systems.
+
+---
+## Introduction
+vllm_simulator is a simulation tool that hijacks a local vLLM installation. It launches a mock inference service—an OpenAI-compatible API server driven by the hijacked vLLM engine—that accepts user requests via real-world trace replay or synthetic load generation using standard benchmarking scripts. vllm_simulator outputs performance metrics identical to those produced by `vllm bench serve`. See **Quick Start** for usage examples.
+
+---
+## Installation
+```bash
+cd tools/vllm-simulator
+pip install .
+```
+
+> **Note**: vllm_simulator hijacks the `vllm` package at runtime through class-level hooks, so a working vLLM installation must be present in the same Python environment.
+
+---
+## Quick Start
+### Step 1: Mock Simulation
+This example runs inference simulation using a synthetic random workload. You may also replay real-world traces (e.g., `--dataset-name timed_trace`).
+
+#### Launch the Simulation Server
+The example uses `NON_BLOCKING` (the default). Run from the project root:
+```bash
+VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE=NON_BLOCKING \
+python3 -m vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server \
+  --model "Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8" \
+  --sim-config-path test/assets/config_vllm.json
+```
+
+> **Notes**:
+> - Use `--sim-config-path` to specify the simulation configuration file, which is equivalent to the system environment variable `VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH`.
+> - The server accepts standard vLLM serving arguments (`--max-model-len`, `--gpu-memory-utilization`, etc.). Do **not** configure TP/EP parallelism here; see the `scheduler` section of the config file below.
+> - `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` defaults to `""` inside the simulator so vLLM's platform detection stays consistent with the simulated environment.
+> - The provided [config file](test/assets/config_vllm.json) is for testing. Adjust the accelerator and other parameters to match your actual deployment scenario for higher fidelity.
+
+#### Run the Benchmark
+For `NON_BLOCKING`, use the simulator's adapted benchmark client:
+```bash
+python3 -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving \
+    --backend openai \
+    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
+    --model "Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8" \
+    --dataset-name random \
+    --request-rate 4 \
+    --random-input-len 1024 \
+    --random-output-len 1024 \
+    --num-prompts 10 \
+    --save-result
+```
+
+The client does not pace requests in real time. Instead, every request carries a logical arrival timestamp (`simulation.created_time`), and the server replays the traffic pattern against its (virtual) simulation clock. Add `--save-result` (optionally with `--result-dir` / `--result-filename`) to persist the result JSON with the simulation metrics.
+
+The following apply only to the NON_BLOCKING benchmark client:
+- Supported backends: `openai` / `vllm` (completions), or `openai-chat` with `--endpoint /v1/chat/completions`. Requests use `stream: false` to return simulation stats.
+- Readiness checks and warmups are excluded from measured stats. Replay needs all requests in flight: omit `--max-concurrency` or set it to at least `--num-prompts`. Probe requests are unsupported.
+- Missing simulation stats are reported as failed requests, not replaced with client-side timings.
+
+For `BLOCKING`, set `VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE=BLOCKING` when launching the same server, then replace the benchmark command above with native `vllm bench serve`.
+
+You have now completed an inference simulation using framework interception.
+
+#### Example Output
+```bash
+============ Serving Benchmark Result ============
+Successful requests:                     10
+Failed requests:                         0
+Request rate configured (RPS):           4.00
+Benchmark duration (s):                  1.15
+Total input tokens:                      10240
+Total generated tokens:                  10240
+Request throughput (req/s):              8.69
+Output token throughput (tok/s):         8901.74
+...
+=============== Simulation Metrics ===============
+Completed requests:                      10
+Simulated duration (s):                  2.53
+Output token throughput (tok/s):         4053.36
+Mean TTFT (ms):                          128.59
+Mean TPOT (ms):                          12.14
+Mean E2EL (ms):                          3431.84
+==================================================
+```
+
+> Latency statistics in "Serving Benchmark Result" use simulated token latencies returned in the responses. Its duration, throughput, and peak concurrency diagnostics still use client wall time. The authoritative simulated duration, throughput, goodput, and KV-cache hit ratios are in "Simulation Metrics" and the saved result JSON (aggregated with `calc_metrics`).
+
+---
+## Usage
+### Mock Simulation (Inference Simulation)
+vllm_simulator uses **dynamic interception** to hijack the execution flow of vLLM, bypassing actual LLM computation:
+
+- **Platform / Worker**: stub CUDA operations and KV-cache allocation so the engine runs on CPU while preserving GPU deployment semantics. The model runner is replaced by a stand-in for Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` is forced; the V1 runner is not modelled).
+- **EngineCore** (`vllm.v1.engine.core.EngineCore`): holds requests in a future queue and dispatches them by `simulation.created_time`; records per-request queueing and prefix-cache hit stats.
+- **Executor** (`UniProcExecutor.execute_model`): accounts the predicted GPU span of each step (AISimulate prediction + sampler/logprobs compensation) and advances the simulation clock.
+- **Per-request stats**: each finished request's stats are returned in its output's `kv_transfer_params["simulation"]` (`RequestOutput` for in-process runners, non-streaming OpenAI responses). Once every received request has finished, the engine resets the virtual clock; no explicit round marker is needed. Per-step iteration stats and optional CPU overhead are logged at DEBUG level without retaining an iteration history.
+
+Key environment variables:
+
+| Variable | Meaning | Default |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH` | Simulation config JSON (see below) | — (required) |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE` | `NON_BLOCKING` (virtual-clock replay) or `BLOCKING` (real-time request handling) | `NON_BLOCKING` |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_MAX_TOKENS` | Force every request's output length (`ignore_eos=True`) | unset |
+
+---
+### Data Collection (Collector)
+The collector runs a **real** vLLM server on GPUs and records per-step and per-request traces, used to calibrate the simulator, train `ml` predictor models, and build `replay` predictor tables. It accepts the same arguments as the `vllm` CLI:
+```bash
+VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_OUTPUT_DIR=/path/to/output \
+python3 -m vllm_simulator.collector.launch_server serve "Qwen/Qwen3-8B" --port 8000
+
+curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/start_profile
+# ... send benchmark traffic ...
+curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/stop_profile
+```
+
+Only traffic between `/start_profile` and `/stop_profile` is recorded. `/stop_profile` writes `rank0.schedule_batch.jsonl` (per-step batch composition and latency) and `requests.jsonl` (per-request timing, KV hits and token ids) synchronously, overwriting the previous window. Under TP only rank 0 is collected.
+
+| Variable | Meaning | Default |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_OUTPUT_DIR` | Export directory | current working directory |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_EXPORT_TOKEN_IDS` | Export `input_ids` / `output_ids` | `1` |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_EXPORT_GZIP` | Write `.jsonl.gz` instead of `.jsonl` | `1` |
+
+---
+### Configuration File Format (`VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH`)
+The config file is a JSON file with three main sections:
+
+- **`platform`**: Hardware settings
+  - `accelerator`: GPU model (e.g., `"h100_sxm"`, `"b300_sxm"`) and `hbm_capacity_gb`
+
+- **`predictor`**: Time prediction module
+  - `name`: predictor type (`"aisimulate"`, `"ml"`, `"replay"` or `"linear"`)
+  - See the **TimePredictor** section below for details
+
+- **`scheduler`**: Parallelism and backend metadata
+  > ⚠️ **Note**: Multi-GPU parallelism (TP/EP) should not be configured at the framework level during server launch. Instead, specify `tp_size` and `ep_size` here; the predictor will simulate parallel execution overhead accordingly.
+  - `backend_name` / `backend_version`: the simulated inference engine and version, used to locate the matching AISimulate performance database (e.g., `"vllm"` / `"0.24.0"`).
+
+**Example Config**:
+```json
+{
+    "platform": {
+        "accelerator": {
+            "name": "h20_sxm",
+            "hbm_capacity_gb": 96
+        }
+    },
+    "predictor": {
+        "name": "aisimulate",
+        "database_mode": "SOL"
+    },
+    "scheduler": {
+        "tp_size": 1,
+        "ep_size": 1,
+        "dp_size": 1,
+        "backend_name": "vllm",
+        "backend_version": "0.24.0"
+    }
+}
+```
+
+---
+## TimePredictor
+### AISimulate
+- Project: <https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate> (successor of AIConfigurator)
+- Install: `pip install aisimulate`. The PyPI package is a stub that fetches the wheel from `https://pypi.nvidia.com`. Uninstall `aiconfigurator` / `aiconfigurator-core` first.
+- Parameters:
+  - `database_path`: (optional) path to custom operator profiling data
+  - `database_mode`: (optional) performance database mode, `"SILICON"` (measured data), `"HYBRID"`, `"EMPIRICAL"` or `"SOL"` (speed-of-light); defaults to `"SILICON"`
+  - `platform.accelerator.name`: device/system name; it should be one of those defined internally in AISimulate
+  - `prefill_scale_factor` / `decode_scale_factor`: optional calibration factors to adjust predicted latency
+
+**Example**:
+```json
+{
+  "name": "aisimulate",
+  "database_path": "path/to/aisimulate/data",
+  "database_mode": "SOL",
+  "prefill_scale_factor": 1.02040816,
+  "decode_scale_factor": 1.01010101
+}
+```
+
+### Linear
+Predicts every non-empty step as `base_ms + per_token_ms * scheduled_tokens`, bypassing any performance model (debugging). KV-cache length is not modelled. Set `per_token_ms` to 0 for a constant per-step latency.
+- Parameters:
+  - `base_ms`: (optional) fixed per-step latency in milliseconds; defaults to 0
+  - `per_token_ms`: (optional) latency per scheduled token in milliseconds; defaults to 0
+
+**Example**:
+```json
+{
+  "name": "linear",
+  "base_ms": 10,
+  "per_token_ms": 0.02
+}
+```

+    created_time: Optional[float] = None
+    queue_start: float = 0.0
+    queue_end: float = 0.0
+    output_length: int = 0
+    input_length: int = 0
+    local_kv_hit_len: int = 0
+    ext_kv_hit_len: int = 0
+    input_ids: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("i"))
+    output_ids: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("i"))

+@dataclass(slots=True)

+    start_timestamp: float = 0.0
+    end_timestamp: float = 0.0
+    forward_mode: int = 0
+    # List of tuples (req_id, extend_input_len, past_kv_len, output_len)
+    requests: list[tuple[str, int, int, int]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    iter_latency: float = 0.0
+    sample_tokens_latency: float = 0.0
+    logprobs_req_count: int = 0
+    logprobs_tokens: int = 0

+# Data is collected only between start_profile and stop_profile.  Worker
+# and EngineCore may live in different processes, so each side keeps its
+# own collecting flag, toggled by its own profile() call.
+_COLLECTING_BATCHES = False
+_COLLECTING_REQUESTS = False
+
+BATCH_INFOS: list[BatchInfos] = []
+
+REQUEST_INFOS: dict[str, RequestInfos] = {}

+# Timing uses CUDA event pairs instead of torch.cuda.synchronize(), which
+# would break async-scheduling overlap and skew the measurement.  Elapsed
+# time is read after vLLM's own sync (AsyncModelRunnerOutput.get_output),
+# so the hook never synchronizes by itself.
+
+
+class _EventTimer:
+    """A start/end pair of timing cuda events for one measured region."""
+
+    __slots__ = ("_start", "_end")
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+        self._end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+
+    def record_start(self) -> None:
+        self._start.record()
+
+    def record_end(self) -> None:
+        self._end.record()
+
+    def elapsed_s(self) -> Optional[float]:
+        """Elapsed seconds, or None if an event has not completed (guards a
+        rare race so it never crashes the engine)."""
+        try:
+            return self._start.elapsed_time(self._end) / 1000.0
+        except RuntimeError:
+            return None
+
+
+# Hands the execute_model (RPC-1) finalizer to the same step's sample_tokens
+# (RPC-2); one slot suffices since the two run back-to-back.
+_PENDING_EXEC: Optional[Callable[[Optional[float]], None]] = None
+
+
+def _finalize_on_get_output(output, finalize):
+    """Run ``finalize`` once vLLM has synced this step's output: inside
+    get_output() for async outputs, immediately otherwise."""
+    original_get_output = getattr(output, "get_output", None)
+    if original_get_output is None:
+        finalize()
+        return output
+
+    def wrapped_get_output(*args, **kwargs):
+        result = original_get_output(*args, **kwargs)
+        finalize()
+        return result
+
+    output.get_output = wrapped_get_output
+    return output

+            for req_id, sched_token in scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens.items():

+

+                scheduler_output.scheduled_cached_reqs.req_ids, 
+                scheduler_output.scheduled_cached_reqs.num_computed_tokens,
+                scheduler_output.scheduled_cached_reqs.num_output_tokens
+            ):

+                batch_req_infos[req_id]["output_len"] = output_token
+

+                batch_req_infos[req.req_id]["output_len"] = (

+                    forward_mode=forward_mode,
+                    # Keep only the last 12 chars of rid.
+                    requests=[

+                            req_info["output_len"],

+                        for rid, req_info in batch_req_infos.items()

+            if max_iterations is not None:
+                profile_kwargs["max_iterations"] = max_iterations
+
+            if is_start:
+                REQUEST_INFOS = {}
+                _COLLECTING_REQUESTS = True
+                return original_profile(self, is_start, profile_prefix, **profile_kwargs)
+
+            _COLLECTING_REQUESTS = False
+            request_infos = REQUEST_INFOS
+            REQUEST_INFOS = {}
+
+            path = f"{OUTPUT_DIR}/requests.jsonl"
+            if EXPORT_GZIP:
+                path += ".gz"
+            with _open_export(path) as f:

+                    row = asdict(req_infos)
+                    if not EXPORT_TOKEN_IDS:

+                        del row["input_ids"]
+                        del row["output_ids"]
+                    f.write(json.dumps(row, cls=CustomJsonEncoder) + "\n")
+            print(f"Request data has been saved to {path}")
+
+            return original_profile(self, is_start, profile_prefix, **profile_kwargs)
+
+        target.profile = wrapped_profile

+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "Scheduler"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler"

+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target) -> None:
+
+        original_add_request = target.add_request
+        original_schedule = target.schedule
+        original_free_request = target._free_request
+
+        # Only requests arriving inside the window are tracked; schedule
+        # and free skip ids absent from REQUEST_INFOS.
+        def wrapped_add_request(self, request):
+            if _COLLECTING_REQUESTS:
+                REQUEST_INFOS[request.request_id] = RequestInfos(
+                    rid=request.request_id,
+                    created_time=request.arrival_time,
+                    queue_start=time.time(),
+                )
+            return original_add_request(self, request)
+
+        def wrapped_schedule(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            scheduler_output = original_schedule(self, *args, **kwargs)
+
+            if scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs:
+                prefill_timestamp = time.time()
+                for new_req_data in scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs:
+                    req_id = new_req_data.req_id
+                    req_info = REQUEST_INFOS.get(req_id)
+                    request = self.requests.get(req_id)
+                    if req_info is None or request is None:
+                        continue
+                    if req_info.queue_end == 0:
+                        req_info.queue_end = prefill_timestamp
+                        req_info.input_length = request.num_prompt_tokens
+                        req_info.output_length = request.max_tokens
+
+                        # The local/external hit split lives on prefill_stats.
+                        req_info.local_kv_hit_len, req_info.ext_kv_hit_len = (
+                            kv_hit_split(request, new_req_data.num_computed_tokens)
+                        )
+
+            return scheduler_output
+
+        def wrapped_free_request(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
+            # Token ids dominate REQUEST_INFOS memory; skip collecting them
+            # entirely when they are not exported.
+            req_info = REQUEST_INFOS.get(request.request_id)
+            if req_info is not None and EXPORT_TOKEN_IDS and request.is_finished():
+                req_info.input_ids = (
+                    array("i", request.prompt_token_ids)
+                    if request.prompt_token_ids is not None
+                    else array("i")
+                )
+                req_info.output_ids = array("i", request.output_token_ids)
+            return original_free_request(self, request, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        target.add_request = wrapped_add_request
+        target.schedule = wrapped_schedule
+        target._free_request = wrapped_free_request

+import builtins

+from vllm_simulator.hook.base_hook import BaseHook, _register_hooks

+def _custom_build_class_(func, name: str, *bases, **kwargs):

+            logger.warning(
+                "Failed to hook class [%s]. Error type: %s, message: %r",
+                name,
+                type(e).__name__,

+            )

+

+"""Online serving benchmark client for the vLLM simulator.
+
+Hijacks ``vllm.benchmarks.serve`` so that:
+
+1. The client never sleeps between requests; each request carries
+   ``simulation.created_time`` and the server replays arrivals from it
+   (see ``C_VLLMEngineCoreHook``).
+2. Non-streaming completions/chat responses return per-request stats in
+   ``kv_transfer_params["simulation"]``. Native benchmark latency metrics use
+   the simulated token latencies; ``calc_metrics`` supplies duration,
+   throughput, and cache-hit metrics.
+
+Usage:
+    python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving [vllm bench serve args...]
+
+Requires the simulator server (``vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server``).
+"""
+
+import inspect
+import json
+import time
+import traceback
+from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from typing import Literal
+
+import aiohttp
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.benchmarks import serve
+from vllm.benchmarks.datasets import SampleRequest
+from vllm.benchmarks.lib import endpoint_request_func as request_funcs
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.utils import calc_metrics
+
+# Enabled by get_request only after readiness checks and warmups finish.
+_REQUEST_STATS: ContextVar[list[dict] | None] = ContextVar(
+    "simulation_request_stats", default=None
+)
+
+
+# Same arrival model as ``serve.get_request``, but the cumulative delay becomes
+# ``simulation.created_time`` instead of a sleep.  Self-timed traces are shifted
+# so the first request starts at zero.
+async def override_get_request(
+    input_requests: list[SampleRequest],
+    request_rate: float,
+    burstiness: float = 1.0,
+    ramp_up_strategy: Literal["linear", "exponential"] | None = None,
+    ramp_up_start_rps: int | None = None,
+    ramp_up_end_rps: int | None = None,
+    self_timed: bool = False,
+) -> AsyncGenerator[tuple[SampleRequest, float], None]:
+    assert burstiness > 0, (
+        f"A positive burstiness factor is expected, but given {burstiness}."
+    )
+    if not isinstance(input_requests, list):
+        input_requests = list(input_requests)
+
+    total_requests = len(input_requests)
+    assert total_requests > 0, "No requests provided."
+    _REQUEST_STATS.set([])
+
+    request_rates: list[float] = []
+    delay_ts: list[float] = []
+
+    if self_timed:
+        input_requests.sort(key=lambda r: r.timestamp or 0.0)
+        first_ts = input_requests[0].timestamp or 0.0
+        for request in input_requests:
+            delay_ts.append((request.timestamp or 0.0) - first_ts)
+            # No notion of RPS for self-timed traces, same as native.
+            request_rates.append(0.0)
+    else:
+        for request_index in range(total_requests):
+            # Reuse the native helper so ramp-up semantics stay in sync.
+            current_request_rate = serve._get_current_request_rate(
+                ramp_up_strategy,
+                ramp_up_start_rps,
+                ramp_up_end_rps,
+                request_index,
+                total_requests,
+                request_rate,
+            )
+            assert current_request_rate > 0.0, (
+                f"Obtained non-positive request rate {current_request_rate}."
+            )
+            request_rates.append(current_request_rate)
+            if current_request_rate == float("inf"):
+                delay_ts.append(0)
+            elif burstiness == float("inf"):
+                # Constant inter-arrival time in the infinite-burstiness limit.
+                delay_ts.append(1.0 / current_request_rate)
+            else:
+                theta = 1.0 / (current_request_rate * burstiness)
+                delay_ts.append(np.random.gamma(shape=burstiness, scale=theta))
+
+        # Cumulative arrival offsets from the first request.
+        for i in range(1, len(delay_ts)):
+            delay_ts[i] += delay_ts[i - 1]
+        if ramp_up_strategy is None and delay_ts[-1] != 0:
+            # Same total-duration normalization as the native generator.
+            target_total_delay_s = total_requests / request_rate
+            normalize_factor = target_total_delay_s / delay_ts[-1]
+            delay_ts = [delay * normalize_factor for delay in delay_ts]
+
+    for request_index, request in enumerate(input_requests):
+        # vllm_xargs is the only path into SamplingParams.extra_args; values
+        # must be scalars/lists, hence the JSON string.
+        overrides = dict(request.request_overrides or {})
+        overrides["vllm_xargs"] = {
+            **overrides.get("vllm_xargs", {}),
+            "simulation": json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "created_time": delay_ts[request_index],
+                    "total_request": total_requests,
+                }
+            ),
+        }
+        request.request_overrides = overrides
+        yield request, request_rates[request_index]
+
+
+async def async_request_simulation(
+    request_func_input: request_funcs.RequestFuncInput,
+    session: aiohttp.ClientSession,
+    pbar=None,
+) -> request_funcs.RequestFuncOutput:
+    """Return simulated token timings from a non-streaming response."""
+    output = request_funcs.RequestFuncOutput(
+        prompt_len=request_func_input.prompt_len, start_time=time.perf_counter()
+    )
+    rows = _REQUEST_STATS.get()
+    try:
+        api_url = request_func_input.api_url
+        is_chat = api_url.endswith("/chat/completions")
+        request_funcs._validate_api_url(api_url, "Simulation API", "completions")
+        payload = {
+            "model": request_func_input.model_name or request_func_input.model,
+        }
+        if is_chat:
+            payload["messages"] = (
+                request_func_input.chat_messages
+                if request_func_input.chat_messages is not None
+                else request_funcs._get_chat_messages(request_func_input)
+            )
+            payload["max_completion_tokens"] = request_func_input.output_len
+        else:
+            payload.update(
+                prompt=request_func_input.prompt,
+                repetition_penalty=1.0,
+                max_tokens=request_func_input.output_len,
+                logprobs=request_func_input.logprobs,
+            )
+        request_funcs._update_payload_common(payload, request_func_input)
+        payload["stream"] = False
+        payload.pop("stream_options", None)
+        if payload.get("n", 1) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("Simulation stats require n=1.")
+
+        # Readiness checks and warmups are independent one-request rounds.
+        # Override any metadata left on a reused dataset by an earlier run.
+        if rows is None:
+            payload["vllm_xargs"] = {
+                **payload.get("vllm_xargs", {}),
+                "simulation": json.dumps({"created_time": 0, "total_request": 1}),
+            }
+        headers = request_funcs._get_headers("application/json")
+        request_funcs._update_headers_common(headers, request_func_input)
+        async with session.post(api_url, json=payload, headers=headers) as response:
+            if response.status != 200:
+                output.error = f"HTTP {response.status}: {await response.text()}"
+                return output
+            data = await response.json()
+
+        stats = (data.get("kv_transfer_params") or {}).get("simulation")
+        if not isinstance(stats, dict) or not stats.get("gen_token_latencies"):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Response has no simulation request stats; use the simulator server."
+            )
+        if len(data["choices"]) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("Simulation stats require a single prompt and choice.")
+        choice = data["choices"][0]
+        output.generated_text = (
+            choice["message"].get("content") if is_chat else choice.get("text")
+        ) or ""
+        usage = data["usage"]
+        output.prompt_len = usage["prompt_tokens"]
+        output.output_tokens = usage["completion_tokens"]
+        latencies = stats["gen_token_latencies"]
+        output.ttft = latencies[0]
+        output.itl = latencies[1:]
+        output.latency = sum(latencies)
+        output.tpot = float(np.mean(output.itl)) if output.itl else 0.0
+        output.success = True
+        if rows is not None:
+            rows.append(
+                {
+                    **stats,
+                    "input_length": output.prompt_len,
+                    "output_length": output.output_tokens,
+                }
+            )
+    except Exception:
+        output.error = traceback.format_exc()
+    finally:
+        if pbar is not None:
+            pbar.update(1)
+    return output
+
+
+# Native latency calculations already consume the simulated RequestFuncOutput.
+# Only wall-clock duration/throughputs and simulation-only metrics need replacing.
+_BASE_RESULT_KEYS = {
+    "duration": "duration",
+    "completed": "completed",
+    "total_input": "total_input_tokens",
+    "total_output": "total_output_tokens",
+    "request_throughput": "request_throughput",
+    "output_throughput": "output_throughput",
+    "total_throughput": "total_token_throughput",
+}
+
+# Simulation-only stats worth keeping in the result json.
+_EXTRA_RESULT_KEYS = (
+    "num_requests",
+    "input_throughput",
+    "mean_queue_ms",
+    "max_itl_ms",
+    "prompt_tokens_cached_ratio",
+    "prompt_tokens_local_cache_hit_ratio",
+    "prompt_tokens_external_kv_transfer_ratio",
+)
+
+
+def _apply_simulation_metrics(result: dict, sim: dict) -> None:
+    if result.get("request_goodput") is not None:
+        result["request_goodput"] *= result["duration"] / sim["duration"]
+    for sim_key, result_key in _BASE_RESULT_KEYS.items():
+        result[result_key] = sim[sim_key]
+    for key in _EXTRA_RESULT_KEYS:
+        if key in sim:
+            result[key] = sim[key]
+
+
+original_benchmark = serve.benchmark
+
+
+async def wrapped_benchmark(*args, **kwargs):
+    options = inspect.signature(original_benchmark).bind(*args, **kwargs)
+    options.apply_defaults()
+    backend = options.arguments["endpoint_type"]
+    if backend not in ("openai", "vllm", "openai-chat"):
+        raise ValueError("Simulation supports openai, vllm, and openai-chat backends.")
+    if (backend == "openai-chat") != options.arguments["api_url"].endswith(
+        "/chat/completions"
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Use --endpoint /v1/chat/completions for openai-chat, "
+            "or /v1/completions for openai/vllm."
+        )
+    concurrency = options.arguments["max_concurrency"]
+    if concurrency and concurrency < len(options.arguments["input_requests"]):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Simulation replay needs all requests in flight; omit --max-concurrency "
+            "or set it to at least the number of requests."
+        )
+    if options.arguments["probe_request_rate"]:
+        raise ValueError("Simulation replay does not support probe requests.")
+
+    token = _REQUEST_STATS.set(None)
+    try:
+        result = await original_benchmark(*args, **kwargs)
+        rows = _REQUEST_STATS.get() or []
+    finally:
+        _REQUEST_STATS.reset(token)
+    if not rows:
+        raise RuntimeError("No simulation request stats returned by the benchmark.")
+
+    sim_metrics = calc_metrics(rows)
+    _apply_simulation_metrics(result, sim_metrics)
+
+    print("{s:{c}^{n}}".format(s=" Simulation Metrics ", n=50, c="="))
+    print(f"{'Completed requests:':<40} {sim_metrics['completed']:<10}")
+    for label, key in (
+        ("Simulated duration (s):", "duration"),
+        ("Output token throughput (tok/s):", "output_throughput"),
+        ("Mean TTFT (ms):", "mean_ttft_ms"),
+        ("Mean TPOT (ms):", "mean_tpot_ms"),
+        ("Mean E2EL (ms):", "mean_e2e_latency_ms"),
+    ):
+        print(f"{label:<40} {sim_metrics[key]:<10.2f}")
+    print("=" * 50)
+    return result
+
+
+for backend in ("openai", "vllm", "openai-chat"):
+    serve.ASYNC_REQUEST_FUNCS[backend] = async_request_simulation
+serve.get_request = override_get_request
+serve.benchmark = wrapped_benchmark
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+
+    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser(
+        description="vLLM simulator online serving benchmark "
+        "(hijacked `vllm bench serve`)"
+    )
+    serve.add_cli_args(parser)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    serve.main(args)

+import asyncio
+import math
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from collections import Counter
+
+import numpy as np

+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.bench_config import BenchmarkConfig

+from vllm_simulator.simulation.manager import Envs
+
+
+class BaseWorker(ABC):
+    def __init__(self, name: str):
+        self.name = name
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    async def async_generate(self, req: GenericRequest) -> dict:
+        """Run one request to completion and return its RequestStats."""
+        pass
+
+    async def flush_cache(self):
+        pass
+
+    def shutdown(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class BaseBenchmarkRunner(ABC):
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
+        # Worker's name -> requests
+        self.lb_routing_records: dict[str, list[GenericRequest]] = {}
+        # Per-request stats of the last benchmark() call.
+        self.request_stats: list[dict] = []
+
+    @property
+    @abstractmethod
+    def all_workers(self) -> list[BaseWorker]:
+        pass
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    async def async_benchmark(
+        self, benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig, requests: list[GenericRequest]
+    ) -> dict:
+        pass
+
+    def benchmark(
+        self, benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig, requests: list[GenericRequest]
+    ) -> dict:
+        return self.loop.run_until_complete(
+            self.async_benchmark(benchmark_config, requests)
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate_workers(workers: list[BaseWorker]) -> None:
+        if not workers:
+            raise ValueError("At least one worker is required")
+        duplicates = [
+            name
+            for name, count in Counter(w.name for w in workers).items()
+            if count > 1
+        ]
+        if duplicates:
+            raise ValueError(f"Worker names must be unique: {duplicates}")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate_request_stats(
+        stats: dict | None, *, expected_rid: str | None = None
+    ) -> dict:
+        if not isinstance(stats, dict):
+            raise RuntimeError("Worker returned no request stats")
+        rid = stats.get("rid")
+        if not isinstance(rid, str) or not rid:
+            raise RuntimeError("Request stats have no request id")
+        if expected_rid is not None and rid != expected_rid:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Request stats id mismatch: expected {expected_rid}, got {rid}"
+            )
+        latencies = stats.get("gen_token_latencies")
+        if not isinstance(latencies, list) or not latencies:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Request {rid} has no generated-token latencies")
+        if not all(
+            isinstance(value, (int, float)) and math.isfinite(value) and value >= 0
+            for value in latencies
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Request {rid} has invalid generated-token latencies")
+        output_length = stats.get("output_length")
+        if output_length != len(latencies):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Request {rid} expected {output_length} output tokens, "
+                f"but has {len(latencies)} latency records"
+            )
+        return stats
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _duration_start_time(stats: list[dict]) -> float:
+        if Envs.simulation_mode() != "BLOCKING" or not stats:
+            return 0.0
+        return min(float(item["created_time"]) for item in stats)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _assign_created_time(
+        requests: list[GenericRequest], benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig
+    ) -> None:
+        """Set each request's logical arrival time."""
+        arrival = 0
+        for req in requests:
+            if benchmark_config.ignore_request_timestamp:
+                created_time = arrival
+                arrival += np.random.exponential(1.0 / benchmark_config.request_rate)
+            else:
+                created_time = req.custom_params.get("created_time", 0)
+            req.custom_params["created_time"] = created_time
+
+    def _record_routing(self, worker: BaseWorker, req: GenericRequest) -> None:
+        self.lb_routing_records.setdefault(worker.name, []).append(req)
+
+    def get_request_stats(self) -> list[dict]:
+        return self.request_stats
+
+    def get_lb_routing_records(self) -> dict[str, list[GenericRequest]]:
+        return self.lb_routing_records
+
+    def flush_cache(self):
+        async def _flush():
+            for worker in self.all_workers:
+                await worker.flush_cache()
+
+        self.loop.run_until_complete(_flush())
+
+    def shutdown(self):
+        for worker in self.all_workers:
+            worker.shutdown()
+        self._close_loop()
+
+    def _close_loop(self):
+        """Drain tasks left on the runner loop (e.g. AsyncLLM output handlers)
+        and close it, so they are not destroyed pending on a closed loop."""
+        loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop = self.loop
+        if loop.is_closed():
+            return
+        pending = asyncio.all_tasks(loop)
+        for task in pending:
+            task.cancel()
+        if pending:
+            loop.run_until_complete(asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True))
+        loop.run_until_complete(loop.shutdown_asyncgens())
+        loop.close()

+"""PD-disaggregated benchmark runner for vLLM simulation workers.
+
+Mirrors vLLM's PD proxy flow: each request first runs on a prefill worker
+with ``max_tokens=1``, then on a decode worker with the original output
+length.  Decode workers must be configured with the DecodeBenchConnector
+(``kv_transfer_config={"kv_connector": "DecodeBenchConnector",
+"kv_role": "kv_both"}``) so the prompt KV is treated as already transferred
+and only the last prompt token is recomputed.  The transfer itself is
+modelled as instantaneous.
+
+Per-request stats come back from each engine with the finished request, so
+the decode phase starts after every prefill has finished: the prefill finish
+time becomes the decode request's ``created_time``.
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import dataclasses
+import uuid
+from collections import Counter
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.base_runner import (
+    BaseBenchmarkRunner,
+    BaseWorker,
+)
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.bench_config import BenchmarkConfig
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.load_balance import (
+    LoadBalancingPolicy,
+    RoundRobinPolicy,
+)
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.request import GenericRequest
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.utils import calc_metrics
+from vllm_simulator.utils.logger import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+class PDDisaggBenchmarkRunner(BaseBenchmarkRunner):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        prefill_workers: list[BaseWorker],
+        decode_workers: list[BaseWorker],
+        prefill_lb_proxy: LoadBalancingPolicy | None = None,
+        decode_lb_proxy: LoadBalancingPolicy | None = None,
+    ):
+        if not prefill_workers or not decode_workers:
+            raise ValueError("PD benchmarks require prefill and decode workers")
+        BaseBenchmarkRunner._validate_workers(prefill_workers + decode_workers)
+        super().__init__()
+        self.prefill_workers = prefill_workers
+        self.decode_workers = decode_workers
+        self.prefill_lb_proxy = prefill_lb_proxy or RoundRobinPolicy()
+        self.decode_lb_proxy = decode_lb_proxy or RoundRobinPolicy()
+        self.prefill_lb_proxy.init_workers(prefill_workers)
+        self.decode_lb_proxy.init_workers(decode_workers)
+
+        # Per-phase stats of the last benchmark() call, keyed by rid.
+        self.prefill_stats: dict[str, dict] = {}
+        self.decode_stats: dict[str, dict] = {}
+
+    @property
+    def all_workers(self) -> list[BaseWorker]:
+        return self.prefill_workers + self.decode_workers
+
+    def _pair_request(self, req: GenericRequest):
+        """Pair a request with its prefill and decode workers."""
+        prefill_worker = self.prefill_lb_proxy.select_worker(self.prefill_workers, req)
+        decode_worker = self.decode_lb_proxy.select_worker(self.decode_workers, req)
+        if (
+            prefill_worker not in self.prefill_workers
+            or decode_worker not in self.decode_workers
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError("Load-balancing policy returned an unknown PD worker")
+        self._record_routing(prefill_worker, req)
+        self._record_routing(decode_worker, req)
+
+        # Shared id joins the two engines' request stats.
+        req.custom_params["request_id"] = uuid.uuid4().hex
+        req.custom_params["prefill_worker"] = prefill_worker
+        req.custom_params["decode_worker"] = decode_worker
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _phase_request(
+        req: GenericRequest, total_request: int, **overrides
+    ) -> GenericRequest:
+        """Per-phase copy of a request.
+
+        ``total_request`` is the number of requests routed to the target
+        worker: NON_BLOCKING engines start dispatching only after receiving
+        that many requests.
+        """
+        custom_params = {
+            **req.custom_params,
+            "total_request": total_request,
+            **overrides.pop("custom_params", {}),
+        }
+        return dataclasses.replace(req, custom_params=custom_params, **overrides)
+
+    async def _run_phase(
+        self, role: str, phase_requests: list[GenericRequest]
+    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
+        """Run one phase to completion and return its stats keyed by rid."""
+        results = await asyncio.gather(
+            *(req.custom_params[role].async_generate(req) for req in phase_requests)
+        )
+        stats_by_id = {}
+        for req, stats in zip(phase_requests, results):
+            expected_rid = req.custom_params["request_id"]
+            stats = self._validate_request_stats(stats, expected_rid=expected_rid)
+            if expected_rid in stats_by_id:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"Duplicate stats for request {expected_rid}")
+            stats_by_id[expected_rid] = stats
+        return stats_by_id
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _merge_request_stats(
+        req: GenericRequest, prefill_stat: dict, decode_stat: dict
+    ) -> dict:
+        """Merge P/D stats as seen by a client of vLLM's PD proxy.
+
+        The client only receives the decode stream, so the first token
+        latency spans the whole prefill plus the decode instance's first
+        step; later token latencies are the decode instance's.
+        """
+        prefill_latencies = prefill_stat["gen_token_latencies"]
+        decode_latencies = decode_stat["gen_token_latencies"]
+        gen_token_latencies = [
+            sum(prefill_latencies) + decode_latencies[0]
+        ] + decode_latencies[1:]
+
+        return {
+            "rid": prefill_stat["rid"],
+            "prefill_worker": req.custom_params["prefill_worker"].name,
+            "decode_worker": req.custom_params["decode_worker"].name,
+            "created_time": prefill_stat["created_time"],
+            "queue_start": prefill_stat["queue_start"],
+            "queue_end": prefill_stat["queue_end"],
+            "last_event_time": decode_stat["last_event_time"],
+            "input_length": prefill_stat["input_length"],
+            "output_length": decode_stat["output_length"],
+            # The prefix cache only matters on the prefill worker; the
+            # decode worker's external hit is the simulated transfer.
+            "local_kv_hit_len": prefill_stat["local_kv_hit_len"],
+            "ext_kv_hit_len": prefill_stat["ext_kv_hit_len"],
+            "gen_token_latencies": gen_token_latencies,
+        }
+
+    async def async_benchmark(
+        self,
+        benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig,
+        requests: list[GenericRequest],
+    ):
+        self.request_stats = []
+        self._assign_created_time(requests, benchmark_config)
+        logger.info(f"Created {len(requests)} PD disagg request tasks.")
+
+        for req in requests:
+            self._pair_request(req)
+
+        # Phase 1: prefill only (first token), as vLLM's PD proxy does.
+        prefill_counts = Counter(
+            req.custom_params["prefill_worker"] for req in requests
+        )
+        self.prefill_stats = prefill_stats = await self._run_phase(
+            "prefill_worker",
+            [
+                self._phase_request(
+                    req,
+                    prefill_counts[req.custom_params["prefill_worker"]],
+                    output_length=1,
+                )
+                for req in requests
+            ],
+        )
+
+        # Phase 2: decode, arriving when the prefill finishes.
+        paired = [
+            (req, prefill_stats[req.custom_params["request_id"]]) for req in requests
+        ]
+
+        decode_counts = Counter(req.custom_params["decode_worker"] for req, _ in paired)
+        self.decode_stats = decode_stats = await self._run_phase(
+            "decode_worker",
+            [
+                self._phase_request(
+                    req,
+                    decode_counts[req.custom_params["decode_worker"]],
+                    custom_params={
+                        "created_time": prefill_stat["last_event_time"],
+                        "queue_start": prefill_stat["last_event_time"],
+                    },
+                )
+                for req, prefill_stat in paired
+            ],
+        )
+
+        for req, prefill_stat in paired:
+            decode_stat = decode_stats[req.custom_params["request_id"]]
+            merged = self._merge_request_stats(req, prefill_stat, decode_stat)
+            self.request_stats.append(self._validate_request_stats(merged))
+
+        return calc_metrics(
+            self.request_stats, self._duration_start_time(self.request_stats)
+        )

+"""Requests for the offline benchmark runners.
+
+Workloads come from ``vllm.benchmarks.datasets``; ``from_sample_requests``
+converts their samples.  Import those datasets after the simulator hooks are
+installed (i.e. after ``vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.vllm_worker``).
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Iterable, Optional
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.benchmarks.datasets import SampleRequest
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class GenericRequest:
+    prompt: Optional[str] = None
+    token_ids: Optional[list[int]] = None
+    input_length: int = -1
+    output_length: int = -1
+    custom_params: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # Extra args used as API request parameters when sending the request
+    extra_args: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        if self.prompt is None and self.token_ids is None:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid Request")
+
+
+def from_sample_requests(
+    samples: Iterable["SampleRequest"],
+) -> list[GenericRequest]:
+    """Convert ``vllm.benchmarks.datasets`` samples for the offline runners.
+
+    A sample timestamp becomes ``created_time``.  Only single text or
+    token-id prompts are supported.
+    """
+    requests = []
+    for sample in samples:
+        if sample.multi_modal_data is not None or sample.lora_request is not None:
+            raise ValueError("Multimodal and LoRA samples are not supported")
+        prompt = sample.prompt
+        if isinstance(prompt, str):
+            req = GenericRequest(prompt=prompt)
+        elif isinstance(prompt, list) and all(isinstance(t, int) for t in prompt):
+            req = GenericRequest(token_ids=list(prompt))
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported prompt type: {type(prompt).__name__}")
+        req.input_length = sample.prompt_len
+        req.output_length = sample.expected_output_len
+        if sample.timestamp is not None:
+            req.custom_params["created_time"] = sample.timestamp
+        requests.append(req)
+    return requests

+"""
+Engine-core hooks that drive one simulated engine step:
+
+- C_VLLMEngineCoreHook: readiness-based request dispatch, BLOCKING-mode
+  request stats, returning finished requests' stats on their outputs and
+  resetting the round state once the engine drains.
+- C_VLLMSchedulerHook: counts parked requests as unfinished so the busy
+  loop keeps stepping.
+- C_VLLMExecutorHook: inits the time predictor, accounts the predicted GPU
+  span at execute_model, records queue/hit and per-token stats, and logs
+  per-step iteration stats at DEBUG level.
+
+The hooks share the module-level request stats.
+"""
+
+import heapq
+import json
+import math
+import time
+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
+
+from vllm_simulator.hook import BaseHook
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.manager import ConfigManager, Envs, StateManager
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.types import (
+    IterationStats,
+    RequestStats,
+    SimulationMode,
+)
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.utils import kv_hit_split
+from vllm_simulator.time_predictor import ScheduleBatch, ScheduleRequest
+from vllm_simulator.utils import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+# When set, overrides max_tokens (with ignore_eos) for every request.
+_MAX_TOKENS = Envs.max_tokens()
+_SIM_MODE = SimulationMode(Envs.simulation_mode())
+
+# Per-request stats keyed by request id; one engine per process.
+_REQUEST_STATS: dict[str, RequestStats] = {}
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class _CPUOverheadStep:
+    predictor_time: float = 0.0
+    emitted: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+def _new_request_stats(request, created_time, queue_start, last_event_time):
+    """Initialize the RequestStats entry; hit fields are set at queue_end."""
+    rid = request.request_id
+    st = _REQUEST_STATS.setdefault(rid, RequestStats(rid=rid))
+    st.created_time = created_time
+    st.queue_start = queue_start
+    st.queue_end = -1
+    st.gen_token_latencies = []
+    st.last_event_time = last_event_time
+    st.input_length = request.num_prompt_tokens
+    st.output_length = request.max_tokens
+    return st
+
+
+def _attach_request_stats(engine_core_outputs) -> None:
+    """Hand finished requests' stats to the frontend.
+
+    kv_transfer_params is the only free-form per-request field carried
+    end-to-end (RequestOutput and non-streaming OpenAI responses).
+    """
+    for outputs in engine_core_outputs.values():
+        for output in outputs.outputs:
+            if not output.finished:
+                continue
+            st = _REQUEST_STATS.pop(output.request_id, None)
+            if st is not None:
+                output.kv_transfer_params = {
+                    **(output.kv_transfer_params or {}),
+                    "simulation": asdict(st),
+                }
+
+
+def _end_round_if_drained(scheduler) -> None:
+    """Reset the per-round state once every received request has finished.
+
+    Replaces an explicit round marker: the virtual clock restarts from 0 for
+    the next round's created_times.  Skipped while a NON_BLOCKING round is
+    still being received.
+    """
+    dispatcher = ReqDispatcher()
+    if scheduler.has_unfinished_requests() or (
+        dispatcher.seq_counter and not dispatcher.all_received
+    ):
+        return
+    # Leftovers are aborted requests only.
+    _REQUEST_STATS.clear()
+    StateManager.reset()
+    dispatcher.reset()
+
+
+class ReqDispatcher:
+    """Singleton holding the NON_BLOCKING replay state.
+
+    Requests parked at EngineCore.add_request are released by dispatch()
+    at queue_start when supplied, otherwise created_time (the TTFT origin).
+    """
+
+    _instance = None
+    _initialized = False
+
+    def __new__(cls):
+        if cls._instance is None:
+            cls._instance = super().__new__(cls)
+        return cls._instance
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        if self.__class__._initialized:
+            return
+        # (dispatch_time, seq, request, request_wave, created_time).
+        self.future_queue: list[tuple[float, int, object, int, float]] = []
+        self.seq_counter = 0
+        self.total_expected = float("inf")
+        self.all_received = False
+        # Captured once at hook install (single engine per process)
+        self.original_core_add_request = None
+        # Live Scheduler, read by C_VLLMExecutorHook.
+        self.scheduler = None
+        self.cpu_step: _CPUOverheadStep | None = None
+        self.__class__._initialized = True
+
+    def reset(self):
+        self.future_queue.clear()
+        self.seq_counter = 0
+        self.total_expected = float("inf")
+        self.all_received = False
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.future_queue)
+
+    def has_next(self) -> bool:
+        return len(self.future_queue) > 0
+
+    def next_req_dispatch_time(self) -> float:
+        return self.future_queue[0][0]
+
+    def add(
+        self,
+        request,
+        request_wave: int,
+        created_time: float,
+        queue_start: float | None = None,
+    ):
+        """Park a request until its recorded engine-entry time.
+
+        Pretokenized replay skips frontend preparation and input delivery.
+        Using queue_start preserves that delay; dispatching at created_time
+        would make the request eligible too early. This overhead can be tens
+        of milliseconds: significant for short TTFTs, but often negligible
+        when TTFT is on the order of seconds.
+        created_time remains the TTFT origin and the dispatch fallback when
+        queue_start is absent.
+        """
+        dispatch_time = created_time if queue_start is None else queue_start
+        if (
+            not math.isfinite(created_time)
+            or not math.isfinite(dispatch_time)
+            or dispatch_time < created_time
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Request times must be finite and queue_start >= arrival")
+        heapq.heappush(
+            self.future_queue,
+            (dispatch_time, self.seq_counter, request, request_wave, created_time),
+        )
+        self.seq_counter += 1
+
+        if self.seq_counter >= self.total_expected:
+            self.all_received = True
+            logger.info(
+                "All %d requests received. Starting simulation.",
+                self.total_expected,
+            )
+
+    def dispatch(self, engine_core):
+        """Re-submit due parked requests through the native add_request."""
+        current_time = StateManager.get_global_clock()
+        while self.future_queue and self.future_queue[0][0] <= current_time:
+            _, _, request, request_wave, created_time = heapq.heappop(
+                self.future_queue
+            )
+            _new_request_stats(
+                request,
+                created_time=created_time,
+                queue_start=current_time,
+                last_event_time=created_time,
+            )
+            self.original_core_add_request(engine_core, request, request_wave)
+
+
+class C_VLLMSchedulerHook(BaseHook):
+    """Count parked requests as unfinished.
+
+    The busy loop queries the Scheduler directly, so without this it would
+    go idle and never dispatch.  has_unfinished_requests / has_requests
+    derive from get_num_unfinished_requests.
+    """
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "Scheduler"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        original_get_num_unfinished = target.get_num_unfinished_requests
+        target.get_num_unfinished_requests = lambda self: (
+            original_get_num_unfinished(self) + len(ReqDispatcher())
+        )
+
+
+class C_VLLMEngineCoreHook(BaseHook):
+    """Dispatch at supplied queue_start or created_time, retaining TTFT origins.
+
+    Requests are parked ahead of Scheduler.add_request so no connector lookup
+    or block allocation happens before the selected dispatch timestamp.
+
+    Prefix block hashing still runs earlier in preprocess_add_request; it
+    touches no cache state.
+    """
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "EngineCore"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.engine.core"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        original_init = target.__init__
+        original_add_request = target.add_request
+        original_step = target.step
+        dispatcher = ReqDispatcher()
+        dispatcher.original_core_add_request = original_add_request
+
+        def wrapped_init(self, vllm_config, *args, **kwargs):
+            """Reset replay state, stats and the virtual clock."""
+            ReqDispatcher().reset()
+            _REQUEST_STATS.clear()
+            StateManager.reset()
+
+            original_init(self, vllm_config, *args, **kwargs)
+            self._sim_cpu_overhead_enabled = ConfigManager.cpu_overhead_enabled()
+            ReqDispatcher().scheduler = self.scheduler
+
+        def wrapped_add_request(self, request, request_wave=0):
+            """Park NON_BLOCKING simulation requests; forward the rest."""
+            if _MAX_TOKENS is not None:
+                if request.sampling_params is not None:
+                    request.sampling_params.max_tokens = _MAX_TOKENS
+                    request.sampling_params.ignore_eos = True
+                request.max_tokens = _MAX_TOKENS
+
+            created_time = None
+            queue_start = None
+            sp = request.sampling_params
+            if sp is not None and sp.extra_args:
+                sim = sp.extra_args.get("simulation")
+                # JSON-encoded by HTTP clients (see bench_serving).
+                if isinstance(sim, str):
+                    sim = json.loads(sim)
+                if sim:
+                    created_time = sim.get("created_time")
+                    queue_start = sim.get("queue_start")
+                    total = sim.get("total_request")
+                    if total is not None:
+                        dispatcher.total_expected = total
+
+            if _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.BLOCKING:
+                now = time.time()
+                _new_request_stats(
+                    request,
+                    created_time=request.arrival_time,
+                    queue_start=now,
+                    last_event_time=now,
+                )
+            if created_time is None or _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.BLOCKING:
+                original_add_request(self, request, request_wave)
+                return
+
+            dispatcher.add(request, request_wave, created_time, queue_start)
+
+        def wrapped_step(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            """Dispatch due future-queue requests before each engine step;
+            return finished requests' stats on their outputs."""
+            if _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.NON_BLOCKING and dispatcher.all_received:
+                dispatcher.dispatch(self)
+
+                # Idle: jump the virtual clock to the next created_time.
+                if (
+                    not any(self.scheduler.get_request_counts())
+                    and dispatcher.has_next()
+                ):
+                    StateManager.set_global_clock(
+                        dispatcher.next_req_dispatch_time() + 1e-6
+                    )
+                    dispatcher.dispatch(self)
+
+            if (
+                _SIM_MODE != SimulationMode.NON_BLOCKING
+                or not dispatcher.all_received
+                or not getattr(self, "_sim_cpu_overhead_enabled", False)
+            ):
+                result = original_step(self, *args, **kwargs)
+            else:
+                result = step_with_cpu_overhead(self, *args, **kwargs)
+            _attach_request_stats(result[0])
+            _end_round_if_drained(self.scheduler)
+            return result
+
+        def step_with_cpu_overhead(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            # Start after dispatch/idle waits; predictor work is excluded below.
+            step = _CPUOverheadStep()
+            dispatcher.cpu_step = step
+            start = time.perf_counter()
+            try:
+                result = original_step(self, *args, **kwargs)
+            finally:
+                dispatcher.cpu_step = None
+            cpu_overhead = max(time.perf_counter() - start - step.predictor_time, 0.0)
+            StateManager.step_global_clock(cpu_overhead)

+            event_time = StateManager.get_global_clock()
+            for req_id in step.emitted:
+                st = _REQUEST_STATS.get(req_id)
+                if st is not None:
+                    st.gen_token_latencies.append(event_time - st.last_event_time)
+                    st.last_event_time = event_time
+            return result
+
+        target.__init__ = wrapped_init
+        target.add_request = wrapped_add_request
+        target.step = wrapped_step
+
+
+class C_VLLMExecutorHook(BaseHook):
+    """Account the predicted GPU span at UniProcExecutor.execute_model.
+
+    ExecutorWithExternalLauncher inherits the hooked method.
+    """
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "UniProcExecutor"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.executor.uniproc_executor"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        original_init_executor = target._init_executor
+        original_execute_model = target.execute_model
+
+        def wrapped_init_executor(self):
+            # Worker.init_device (inside) resolves the ConfigManager state.
+            original_init_executor(self)
+            self._sim_predictor = ConfigManager.get_inference_time_predictor()
+            logger.info("%s initialized for vLLM.", type(self._sim_predictor).__name__)
+
+        def wrapped_execute_model(self, scheduler_output, *args, **kwargs):
+            num_scheduled_tokens = scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens
+            if not num_scheduled_tokens:
+                return original_execute_model(self, scheduler_output, *args, **kwargs)
+
+            # Clock before this step is accounted.
+            queue_end_time = (
+                time.time()
+                if _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.BLOCKING
+                else StateManager.get_global_clock()
+            )
+            # Scheduled requests stay in Scheduler.requests until
+            # update_from_output.
+            requests = ReqDispatcher().scheduler.requests
+
+            # Pre-step num_computed_tokens, i.e. past_kv_length.
+            new_reqs = scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs
+            num_computed = {r.req_id: r.num_computed_tokens for r in new_reqs}
+            cached = scheduler_output.scheduled_cached_reqs
+            num_computed.update(zip(cached.req_ids, cached.num_computed_tokens))
+
+            for new_req_data in new_reqs:
+                # Resumed requests also arrive here (V2 layout); queue and hit
+                # stats belong to the first schedule only.
+                st = _REQUEST_STATS.get(new_req_data.req_id)
+                if st is not None and st.queue_end == -1:
+                    st.queue_end = queue_end_time
+                    st.local_kv_hit_len, st.ext_kv_hit_len = kv_hit_split(
+                        requests[new_req_data.req_id],
+                        new_req_data.num_computed_tokens,
+                    )
+                    logger.info(
+                        "[HitRate] rid=%s input_len=%d local_hit=%d ext_hit=%d",
+                        st.rid,
+                        st.input_length,
+                        st.local_kv_hit_len,
+                        st.ext_kv_hit_len,
+                    )
+
+            # token_emitted is False for intermediate chunked-prefill steps;
+            # passed to _ModelRunnerStub on scheduler_output.
+            simulation_batch = ScheduleBatch(reqs=[])
+            token_emitted: dict[str, bool] = {}
+            logprobs_tokens = 0
+            for req_id, num_tokens in num_scheduled_tokens.items():
+                request = requests[req_id]
+                past_kv_length = num_computed[req_id]
+                # GPUModelRunnerV2 samples nothing while seq_len < prefill_len
+                # (chunked prefill); num_tokens is prefill_len at (re)admission
+                # and seq_len - 1 while decoding.
+                token_emitted[req_id] = (
+                    past_kv_length + num_tokens >= request.num_tokens
+                )
+                sp = request.sampling_params

+                    logprobs_tokens += num_tokens

+                    ScheduleRequest(
+                        extend_length=num_tokens,
+                        past_kv_length=past_kv_length,
+                    )
+                )

+
+            result = original_execute_model(self, scheduler_output, *args, **kwargs)
+
+            cpu_step = ReqDispatcher().cpu_step
+            predictor_start = time.perf_counter() if cpu_step is not None else 0.0
+            predictor = self._sim_predictor
+            predicted_latency, sample_tokens_latency = predictor.predict_step_time(
+                simulation_batch
+            )
+            predicted_latency = float(predicted_latency)
+            sample_tokens_latency = float(sample_tokens_latency)
+
+            # Logprobs cost missing from a baseline collected without them;
+            # active only with logprobs_cost_us_per_token > 0.
+            logprobs_latency = predictor.logprobs_cost_s_per_token * logprobs_tokens
+
+            # RPC-2 (sample_tokens) span, kept separate from the RPC-1-only
+            # predicted_latency so both stay auditable in DEBUG logs.
+            total_tokens = sum(num_scheduled_tokens.values())
+            if cpu_step is not None:
+                cpu_step.predictor_time += time.perf_counter() - predictor_start
+
+            iter_stats = IterationStats(
+                requests=simulation_batch.request_info(),
