+"""
+CPU stand-in for GPUModelRunnerV2 (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py),
+driven by the native Worker.
+
+KV tensors are one page each; page sizes stay at real model values since
+they are accounting-only.
+"""
+
+import functools
+import os
+
+import torch
+from torch.overrides import TorchFunctionMode
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.manager import ConfigManager
+from vllm_simulator.utils import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+def _noop(*args, **kwargs):
+    """Module-level so it is picklable."""
+    return None
+
+
+class _ModelRunnerStub:
+    """Picklable model_runner stub; other attributes resolve to no-ops."""
+
+    # Read by Worker.execute_model under the V2 runner.
+    is_pooling_model = False
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config, kv_spec: dict):
+        from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.kv_connector import NO_OP_KV_CONNECTOR
+
+        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self._kv_spec = kv_spec
+        self.kv_connector = NO_OP_KV_CONNECTOR
+        self.model_memory_usage = 0
+        # Explicit None (not the __getattr__ no-op) so LLMEngine skips its
+        # model cleanup finalizer.
+        self.model = None
+
+    def get_kv_cache_spec(self):
+        return self._kv_spec
+
+    def get_supported_tasks(self):
+        return ("generate",)
+
+    def initialize_kv_cache(self, kv_cache_config, *args, **kwargs):
+        """Allocate one-page CPU KV tensors and hand them to the V2 KV
+        connector wrapper."""
+        from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.kv_connector import get_kv_connector
+
+        kv_caches: dict = {}
+        for kv_tensor in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors:
+            tensor = torch.zeros(
+                min(kv_tensor.size, 4096), dtype=torch.int8, device="cpu"
+            )
+            for layer_name in kv_tensor.layers:
+                kv_caches[layer_name] = tensor
+        logger.info(
+            "[vLLM Hijack] Allocated %d MINIMAL CPU KV cache tensors "
+            "(num_blocks=%d, simulated_bytes=%d, actual_bytes=4k)",
+            len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors),
+            kv_cache_config.num_blocks,
+            sum(t.size for t in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors),
+        )
+        self.kv_connector = get_kv_connector(self.vllm_config, kv_caches)
+
+    def execute_model(self, scheduler_output, intermediate_tensors=None):
+        """Mock forward inside the V2 KV connector lifecycle.
+
+        Returns the output directly (no sample_tokens RPC); finish_forward
+        is skipped since only HiSparse connectors implement it.
+        """
+        from vllm.v1.outputs import ModelRunnerOutput
+
+        if not scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens:
+            return self.kv_connector.no_forward(scheduler_output)
+
+        self.kv_connector.pre_forward(scheduler_output)
+        kv_connector_output = self.kv_connector.post_forward(
+            scheduler_output.finished_req_ids
+        )
+
+        # Whether each request samples a token this step comes from
+        # C_VLLMExecutorHook (_sim_token_emitted).
+        req_ids = list(scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens)
+        token_emitted = scheduler_output._sim_token_emitted
+        return ModelRunnerOutput(
+            req_ids=req_ids,
+            req_id_to_index={rid: i for i, rid in enumerate(req_ids)},
+            sampled_token_ids=[
+                [1] if token_emitted[rid] else [] for rid in req_ids
+            ],
+            kv_connector_output=kv_connector_output,
+        )
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        if name.startswith('_'):
+            raise AttributeError(name)
+        return _noop
+
+
+class _ForceMetaDevice(TorchFunctionMode):
+    """Redirect explicit ``device=`` arguments to meta; the plain
+    ``torch.device("meta")`` context only fills in a missing device."""
+
+    def __torch_function__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        kwargs = kwargs or {}
+        if kwargs.get("device") is not None:
+            kwargs["device"] = "meta"
+        return func(*args, **kwargs)
+
+
+class _NullCudaStream:
+    """Stands in for torch.cuda.Stream; aux streams are never used on
+    the meta build."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        pass
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _simulated_device_capability():
+    """Capability of the simulated accelerator, read from its
+    AISimulate system spec; A100 when the system is unknown."""
+    import yaml
+    from aisimulate_core.sdk.perf_database import get_systems_paths
+
+    from vllm.platforms.interface import DeviceCapability
+
+    name = ConfigManager.get_accelerator_info().name
+    for path in get_systems_paths():
+        spec_path = os.path.join(path, f"{name}.yaml")
+        if os.path.exists(spec_path):
+            with open(spec_path) as f:
+                sm_version = yaml.safe_load(f)["gpu"]["sm_version"]
+            return DeviceCapability(*divmod(sm_version, 10))
+    return DeviceCapability(8, 0)
+
+
+def build_kv_cache_spec(vllm_config) -> dict:
+    """Derive the KV cache spec like GPUModelRunnerV2: build the model on
+    the meta device and collect its attention layers' specs.
+
+    Built under the simulated TP size so specs describe one rank of the
+    target deployment.  Requires the distributed env (set up in
+    init_device).
+    """
+    import vllm.distributed.parallel_state as ps
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.utils import initialize_model
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+    from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils import get_kv_cache_spec
+
+    # The engine runs at tp=1 (EngineArgs hook); the simulated tp lives in
+    # the simulator scheduler config.
+    sim_tp = ConfigManager.get_scheduler_config().tp_size
+
+    tp_group = ps.get_tp_group()
+    orig_world = tp_group.world_size
+    orig_cfg_tp = vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size
+    orig_oot = current_platform.is_out_of_tree
+    orig_ep = getattr(ps, "_EP", None)
+
+    # Scope-patches for the meta build:
+    # 1. Shard sizes come from get_tp_group().world_size, not
+    #    parallel_config; no communication happens on the meta device.
+    # 2. The unquantized-MoE backend oracle raises UnboundLocalError on
+    #    a platform that is none of cuda/rocm/xpu/cpu.  Out-of-tree
+    #    makes it return (OOT, None); experts_cls is unused here.
+    # 3. _EP exists only if the first engine in the process was MoE.
+    #    Lend it the TP group: MoE layers contribute no KV spec.
+    # 4. Sparse-attention models (DSA, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3) allocate
+    #    buffers with an explicit CUDA device and create aux CUDA
+    #    streams; no CUDA device is visible to the simulator.
+    # 5. Attention backends and quantized kernels are chosen by device
+    #    capability and platform and decide the KV cache layout: build
+    #    (and collect the specs) as CUDA on the simulated accelerator.
+    #    The compute-unit count only sizes kernel workspaces.
+    platform_cls = type(current_platform)
+    platform_patches = {
+        "get_device_capability": classmethod(
+            lambda cls, device_id=0: _simulated_device_capability()
+        ),
+        "is_cuda": lambda self: True,
+        "get_cuda_runtime_major": classmethod(
+            lambda cls: int((torch.version.cuda or "0").split(".")[0])
+        ),
+        "num_compute_units": classmethod(lambda cls, device_id=0: 132),
+    }
+    orig_platform = {
+        name: vars(platform_cls).get(name) for name in platform_patches
+    }
+    orig_stream = torch.cuda.Stream
+    current_platform.is_out_of_tree = lambda: True
+    torch.cuda.Stream = _NullCudaStream
+    for name, attr in platform_patches.items():
+        setattr(platform_cls, name, attr)
+    if ps._EP is None:
+        ps._EP = tp_group
+    if sim_tp > 1:
+        tp_group.world_size = sim_tp
+        vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size = sim_tp
+    try:
+        try:
+            with (
+                set_default_torch_dtype(vllm_config.model_config.dtype),
+                torch.device("meta"),
+                _ForceMetaDevice(),
+            ):
+                initialize_model(vllm_config)
+            # Alignment queries config-derived Mamba shapes; keep simulated TP
+            # active until both block alignment and per-rank specs are resolved.
+            current_platform.update_block_size_for_backend(vllm_config)
+            kv_cache_spec = get_kv_cache_spec(vllm_config)
+        finally:
+            tp_group.world_size = orig_world
+            vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size = orig_cfg_tp
+            current_platform.is_out_of_tree = orig_oot
+            torch.cuda.Stream = orig_stream
+            ps._EP = orig_ep
+    finally:
+        for name, attr in orig_platform.items():
+            if attr is None:
+                delattr(platform_cls, name)
+            else:
+                setattr(platform_cls, name, attr)
+
+    logger.info(
+        "[vLLM Hijack] Built KV cache spec via meta-device model walk: "
+        "%d layers (sim tp=%d)", len(kv_cache_spec), sim_tp,
+    )
+    return kv_cache_spec

+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target_class):
+        iface = sys.modules["vllm.platforms.interface"]
+        PlatformEnum = iface.PlatformEnum
+

+            _enum = PlatformEnum.CUDA

+            dispatch_key = "CUDA"
+

+                return capability <= cls.get_device_capability().to_int()
+
+            @classmethod
+            def check_and_update_config(cls, vllm_config) -> None:
+                parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+                if parallel_config.worker_cls == "auto":

+                pass
+

+                pass
+
+            @classmethod
+            def get_device_name(cls, device_id: int = 0) -> str:
+                return "NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB"
+
+            @classmethod

+                    return AttentionBackendEnum.CPU_ATTN.get_path()
+

+                # cache layout: select like CUDA for the simulated arch.
+                from vllm.platforms.cuda import CudaPlatformBase
+                valid, invalid = CudaPlatformBase.get_valid_backends(
+                    cls.get_device_capability(), attn_selector_config, num_heads
+                )
+                if not valid:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        f"No valid MLA backend for {attn_selector_config}: "
+                        f"{invalid}"
+                    )

+
+            @classmethod

+                # The base Platform imports vllm._C, which CUDA wheels do not
+                # ship; compile passes need the CUDA op registrations.

+                CudaPlatformBase.import_kernels()
+
+            @classmethod
+            def verify_quantization(cls, quant: str) -> None:
+                pass
+
+            @classmethod

+_HOOKS_INSTALLED = False
+
+
+def init_hook():

+    global _HOOKS_INSTALLED
+    if _HOOKS_INSTALLED:

+    import vllm_simulator.hook as vllm_simulator_hook
+    from vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm import (

+    # Fixed NONE_HASH seed so block hashes match across nodes.

+VLLMWorker - AsyncLLM-backed BaseWorker for the simulation benchmarks.
+
+Hooks are installed before importing vLLM.  Stats are recorded in the
+EngineCoreProc child and returned with each finished request's output.

+from vllm.engine.arg_utils import AsyncEngineArgs  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM  # noqa: E402

+# AsyncLLM.from_engine_args requires AsyncEngineArgs; aliased so callers
+# keep using EngineArgs.
+EngineArgs = AsyncEngineArgs
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+def _resolve_prompt(req: GenericRequest):
+    """Resolve prompt from GenericRequest (text or token_ids)."""
+    from vllm import TokensPrompt
+
+    if req.prompt is not None:
+        return req.prompt
+    if req.token_ids is not None:
+        return TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=req.token_ids)
+    raise ValueError("Request must have either prompt or token_ids")
+
+
+class VLLMWorker(BaseWorker):
+    """High-level vLLM worker for simulation benchmarks.
+
+    Accepts a vLLM EngineArgs directly; the EngineArgs hook applies the
+    simulation-fixed settings (parallelism, executor, async scheduling).
+    enforce_eager defaults to True unless set explicitly.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        engine_args: EngineArgs,
+        name: str = "vllm_worker0",
+    ):
+        super().__init__(name)
+
+        if engine_args.enforce_eager == AsyncEngineArgs.enforce_eager:
+            engine_args.enforce_eager = True
+
+        # Construction is safe outside a running event loop: AsyncLLM defers
+        # its output handler to the first generate() call.
+        self._llm = AsyncLLM.from_engine_args(engine_args)
+        logger.info("[VLLMWorker] Initialized with model=%s", engine_args.model)
+
+    async def async_generate(self, req: GenericRequest) -> dict:
+        """Stream a single request through the engine; returns its stats."""
+        # Pass simulation metadata (created_time) via extra_args
+        extra_args = None
+        if req.custom_params:
+            sim_meta = {}
+            if "created_time" in req.custom_params:
+                sim_meta["created_time"] = req.custom_params["created_time"]
+            if "queue_start" in req.custom_params:
+                sim_meta["queue_start"] = req.custom_params["queue_start"]
+            if "total_request" in req.custom_params:
+                sim_meta["total_request"] = req.custom_params["total_request"]
+            if sim_meta:
+                extra_args = {"simulation": sim_meta}
+
+        sp = SamplingParams(
+            max_tokens=req.output_length, ignore_eos=True, extra_args=extra_args
+        )
+        prompt = _resolve_prompt(req)
+        # Callers that join stats across engines (PD) pin the request id;
+        # it is kept verbatim since request-id randomization is disabled.
+        request_id = req.custom_params.get("request_id") or uuid.uuid4().hex
+        req.custom_params["request_id"] = request_id
+
+        final_output = None
+        async for output in self._llm.generate(prompt, sp, request_id=request_id):
+            final_output = output
+
+        params = final_output.kv_transfer_params if final_output else None
+        stats = (params or {}).get("simulation")
+        if stats is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"[VLLMWorker] {self.name}: no stats for {request_id}")
+        return {**stats, "rid": final_output.request_id}
+
+    async def flush_cache(self):
+        """Clear the device prefix cache and the KV connector cache.
+
+        Call between rounds: the reset fails while requests hold blocks.
+        """
+        if not await self._llm.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"[VLLMWorker] {self.name}: cache reset failed")
+
+    def generate(self, req: GenericRequest) -> dict:
+        """Generate output for a single request (sync); returns its stats.
+
+        Only safe as the first generate entrypoint on this worker: AsyncLLM
+        binds its output handler to the loop of the first generate() call.
+        """
+        return asyncio.run(self.async_generate(req))
+
+    def shutdown(self):
+        """Shutdown the vLLM engine and its background process."""
+        self._llm.shutdown()
+        logger.info("[VLLMWorker] Shutting down.")

+class AISimulateTimePredictor(InferTimePredictor):

+        hw: AcceleratorInfo,
+        config: SchedulerConfig,
+        database_path: Optional[str] = None,
+        database_mode: DatabaseMode | str = DatabaseMode.SILICON,
+        prefill_scale_factor: float = 1,
+        decode_scale_factor: float = 1,
+        prefill_min_latency: float = 0,
+        workload_distribution: str = "balanced",

+            database_mode = self._get_database_mode(database_mode)

+        )

+            version=self._resolve_database_version(

+            database_mode=database_mode.name,

+        self,

+        backend: str,
+        version: Optional[str],

+    ) -> str:
+        # AISimulate only serves versions within its queryable slots
+        # (current/previous/next); fall back to the 'current' slot when the
+        # requested version is unlisted.
+        if not version:
+            return "current"
+        try:
+            return resolve_query_version(
+                system, backend, version, systems_paths=systems_paths
+            )
+        except ValueError:
+            resolved = resolve_query_version(
+                system, backend, "current", systems_paths=systems_paths
+            )

+                "AISimulate has no queryable %s/%s on %s, falling back to "
+                "'current' slot %s. Set AIC_ALLOW_UNLISTED_VERSIONS=1 to force "

+            "HYBRID": DatabaseMode.HYBRID,
+            "EMPIRICAL": DatabaseMode.EMPIRICAL,
+            "SOL": DatabaseMode.SOL,
+        }.get(mode.upper(), DatabaseMode.SILICON)
+
+    def ctx_attn_flops_ratio_with_avg(self, reqs: list[ScheduleRequest]) -> float:
+        if len(reqs) == 1:
+            return 1.0
+        mean_past = np.mean([req.past_kv_length for req in reqs])
+        mean_input = np.mean([req.extend_length for req in reqs])
+        avg_flops = (mean_past + mean_past + mean_input) * mean_input / 2 * len(reqs)
+
+        actual_flops = 0
+        for req in reqs:
+            actual_flops += (
+                (req.past_kv_length + req.past_kv_length + req.extend_length)
+                * req.extend_length
+                / 2
+            )
+
+        return actual_flops / avg_flops
+
+    def _run_static(self, runtime_config: RuntimeConfig, mode: str) -> dict:
+        if self.enable_oom_check:
+            summary = self._backend.run_static(
+                self._model, self._database, runtime_config, mode
+            )
+            if mode == "static_gen":
+                return summary.get_generation_latency_dict()
+            return summary.get_context_latency_dict()
+        # faster path: skip building the InferenceSummary
+        results = self._backend._run_static_breakdown(
+            self._model,
+            self._database,
+            runtime_config,
+            mode=mode,
+            include_energy=False,
+        )
+        return results[2] if mode == "static_gen" else results[0]
+
+    def predict_infer_latency_dict(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> dict:
+        # Returns latency details for debugging operators.
+        if batch.is_empty():
+            return {}
+        if batch.is_decode():
+            # Decode: output sequence length (osl) = 2, input sequence length (isl) = mean(past_kv_length)
+            isl = int(np.mean([req.past_kv_length for req in batch.reqs]))
+            runtime_config = RuntimeConfig(batch_size=batch.batch_size, isl=isl, osl=2)
+            return self._run_static(runtime_config, "static_gen")
+
+        # Prefill: output sequence length (osl) = 1, input sequence length (isl) = mean(past_kv + input), prefix = mean(past_kv)
+        mean_past = np.mean([req.past_kv_length for req in batch.reqs])
+        mean_input = np.mean([req.extend_length for req in batch.reqs])
+        isl = int(mean_past + mean_input)
+        prefix = int(mean_past)
+
+        seq_imbalance_correction_scale = self.ctx_attn_flops_ratio_with_avg(batch.reqs)
+        extra_kwargs = (
+            {"seq_imbalance_correction_scale": seq_imbalance_correction_scale}
+            if seq_imbalance_correction_scale >= 0.4

+        )

+            batch_size=batch.batch_size,
+            isl=isl,
+            prefix=prefix,
+            osl=1,
+            **extra_kwargs,
+        )
+        return self._run_static(runtime_config, "static_ctx")
+
+    def predict_infer_time(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> float:
+        latency_dict = self.predict_infer_latency_dict(batch)
+        infer_time = sum(latency_dict.values())
+
+        if batch.is_decode():
+            infer_time *= self.decode_scale_factor
+        else:
+            infer_time = max(
+                infer_time * self.prefill_scale_factor, self.prefill_min_latency
+            )
+
+        return infer_time / 1e3

+"""ML-trained per-iteration latency predictor.
+
+Build a prefill/decode sklearn bundle from collector exports with
+``MLTimePredictor.build_model_from_schedule_batch``. Training and inference
+share the simulator's common ``ScheduleBatch`` feature schema.
+"""
+
+import gzip
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import typing
+import warnings
+
+import joblib
+from sklearn.exceptions import InconsistentVersionWarning
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.types import SchedulerConfig
+from vllm_simulator.spec.accelerator import AcceleratorInfo
+from vllm_simulator.time_predictor.base import (
+    InferTimePredictor,
+    ScheduleBatch,
+    ScheduleRequest,
+)
+from vllm_simulator.utils import get_logger
+
+if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import ModelConfig
+
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+class MLTimePredictor(InferTimePredictor):
+    """Predict a step latency from batch-composition features."""
+
+    FEATURE_NAMES = [
+        "batch_size",
+        "sum_extend",
+        "max_extend",
+        "min_extend",
+        "sum_past",
+        "max_past",
+        "min_past",
+        "sum_extend_x_past",
+        "sum_extend_squared",
+        "sum_past_squared",
+        "sum_attn_flops",
+        "sum_extend_x_max_past",
+        "log1p_sum_past",
+        "log1p_sum_attn_flops",
+        "batch_size_x_sum_extend",
+        "max_past_minus_min_past",
+        "is_decode",
+        "is_prefill",
+    ]
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def build_model_from_schedule_batch(
+        jsonl_paths: str | list[str],
+        output_path: str | None = None,
+    ) -> dict:
+        """Train forward-latency models from collector schedule_batch exports.
+
+        Pure decode (all extend lengths equal 1) and prefill/mixed steps are
+        fitted separately. If either phase is absent, reuse the other model.
+        Labels are RPC-1 iter_latency in seconds; sample_tokens is not fitted.
+
+        Args:
+            jsonl_paths: One JSONL path or several; .gz is auto-detected.
+            output_path: Optional joblib output; use as database_path.
+
+        Returns:
+            A bundle with prefill/decode models and the shared feature schema.
+
+        Raises:
+            ValueError: No scheduled steps or invalid lengths/latencies.
+        """
+        import numpy as np
+        from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
+
+        if isinstance(jsonl_paths, str):
+            jsonl_paths = [jsonl_paths]
+        features, latencies = [], []
+        for path in jsonl_paths:
+            opener = gzip.open if path.endswith(".gz") else open
+            with opener(path, "rt") as source:
+                for line in source:
+                    if not line.strip():
+                        continue
+                    row = json.loads(line)
+                    requests = row.get("requests") or []
+                    if not requests:
+                        continue
+                    if any(
+                        not isinstance(value, int) or value < minimum
+                        for req in requests
+                        for value, minimum in ((req[1], 1), (req[2], 0))
+                    ):
+                        raise ValueError(f"Invalid scheduled lengths in {path}")
+                    batch = ScheduleBatch(
+                        [
+                            ScheduleRequest(extend_length=req[1], past_kv_length=req[2])
+                            for req in requests
+                        ]
+                    )
+                    latency = float(row["iter_latency"])
+                    if not math.isfinite(latency) or latency < 0:
+                        raise ValueError(f"Invalid iter_latency in {path}: {latency}")
+                    features.append(MLTimePredictor._extract_features(batch))
+                    latencies.append(latency)
+        if not features:
+            raise ValueError("Cannot train an ML model without scheduled steps")
+        X, y = np.asarray(features), np.asarray(latencies)
+        is_decode = X[:, -2] == 1
+        models = {}
+        for name, mask in (("prefill", ~is_decode), ("decode", is_decode)):
+            if mask.any():
+                models[name] = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=0).fit(
+                    X[mask], y[mask]
+                )
+                logger.info("Trained %s model on %d steps", name, int(mask.sum()))
+        for name in ("prefill", "decode"):
+            if name not in models:
+                logger.warning("No %s steps; reusing the other phase's model", name)
+                models[name] = next(iter(models.values()))
+        bundle = {**models, "features": list(MLTimePredictor.FEATURE_NAMES)}
+        if output_path:
+            joblib.dump(bundle, output_path)
+            logger.info("ML model written to %s", output_path)
+        return bundle
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        model: "ModelConfig",
+        hw: AcceleratorInfo,
+        config: SchedulerConfig,
+        database_path: str,
+        latency_scale: float = 1.0,
+        logprobs_cost_us_per_token: float = 0.0,
+        sample_tokens_base_ms: float = 0.0,
+        sample_tokens_lo_us_per_token: float = 0.0,
+        sample_tokens_hi_us_per_token: float = 0.0,
+        sample_tokens_breakpoint_tokens: int = 0,
+        **kwargs,

+            raise FileNotFoundError(

+            )
+

+        # the compatibility signal without flooding a 500-tree simulation log.
+        with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as version_warnings:
+            warnings.simplefilter("always", InconsistentVersionWarning)
+            bundle = joblib.load(database_path)
+        if version_warnings:
+            logger.warning(
+                "MLTimePredictor loaded a model produced by another sklearn "
+                "version (%d compatibility warnings suppressed)",
+                len(version_warnings),
+            )
+        if isinstance(bundle, dict) and "prefill" in bundle and "decode" in bundle:
+            self._prefill_model = bundle["prefill"]
+            self._decode_model = bundle["decode"]
+            saved_features = bundle.get("features", self.FEATURE_NAMES)
+        elif isinstance(bundle, dict) and "model" in bundle:
+            self._prefill_model = bundle["model"]
+            self._decode_model = bundle["model"]
+            saved_features = bundle.get("features", self.FEATURE_NAMES)
+        else:
+            self._prefill_model = bundle
+            self._decode_model = bundle
+            saved_features = self.FEATURE_NAMES
+
+        if list(saved_features) != self.FEATURE_NAMES:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "MLTimePredictor feature schema mismatch: "
+                f"saved={list(saved_features)!r}, expected={self.FEATURE_NAMES!r}"
+            )
+
+        self._latency_scale = float(latency_scale)
+        # Extra per-token cost of logprobs requests, for baselines collected
+        # without logprobs.  Must be calibrated separately.
+        self.logprobs_cost_s_per_token = float(logprobs_cost_us_per_token) / 1e6

+        # only.  Hinge function of the step's scheduled tokens:
+        #
+        #   sample_tokens_s = base + a_lo * tt + (a_hi - a_lo) * max(0, tt - s)
+        #
+        # Kept separate from the label prediction; disabled when all terms
+        # are 0.
+        self.sample_tokens_base_s = float(sample_tokens_base_ms) / 1e3
+        self.sample_tokens_lo_s_per_token = float(sample_tokens_lo_us_per_token) / 1e6
+        self.sample_tokens_hi_s_per_token = float(sample_tokens_hi_us_per_token) / 1e6
+        self.sample_tokens_breakpoint_tokens = max(
+            0, int(sample_tokens_breakpoint_tokens)
+        )
+        self._sample_tokens_enabled = (
+            self.sample_tokens_base_s > 0.0
+            or self.sample_tokens_lo_s_per_token > 0.0
+            or self.sample_tokens_hi_s_per_token > 0.0
+        )
+        logger.info(
+            "MLTimePredictor loaded from %s (prefill=%s, decode=%s, "
+            "n_features=%d, latency_scale=%.4f)",
+            database_path,
+            type(self._prefill_model).__name__,
+            type(self._decode_model).__name__,
+            len(saved_features),
+            self._latency_scale,
+        )
+        if self._sample_tokens_enabled:
+            logger.info(
+                "MLTimePredictor sample_tokens compensation enabled: "
+                "base=%.3fms a_lo=%.4fus/token a_hi=%.4fus/token "
+                "breakpoint=%d tokens",
+                self.sample_tokens_base_s * 1e3,
+                self.sample_tokens_lo_s_per_token * 1e6,
+                self.sample_tokens_hi_s_per_token * 1e6,
+                self.sample_tokens_breakpoint_tokens,
+            )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _extract_features(batch: ScheduleBatch) -> list[float]:
+        exts = [req.extend_length for req in batch.reqs]
+        pasts = [req.past_kv_length for req in batch.reqs]
+
+        batch_size = len(exts)
+        sum_extend = sum(exts)
+        sum_past = sum(pasts)
+        max_extend = max(exts)
+        min_extend = min(exts)
+        max_past = max(pasts)
+        min_past = min(pasts)
+        sum_attn_flops = sum(
+            extend * (past + extend / 2) for extend, past in zip(exts, pasts)
+        )
+
+        return [
+            batch_size,
+            sum_extend,
+            max_extend,
+            min_extend,
+            sum_past,
+            max_past,
+            min_past,
+            sum(extend * past for extend, past in zip(exts, pasts)),
+            sum(extend * extend for extend in exts),
+            sum(past * past for past in pasts),
+            sum_attn_flops,
+            sum_extend * max_past,
+            math.log1p(sum_past),
+            math.log1p(sum_attn_flops),
+            batch_size * sum_extend,
+            max_past - min_past,
+            int(all(extend == 1 for extend in exts)),
+            int(any(extend > 1 for extend in exts)),
+        ]
+
+    def predict_infer_time(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> float:
+        if batch.is_empty():
+            return 0.0
+
+        features = self._extract_features(batch)
+        is_decode = features[-2] == 1
+        model = self._decode_model if is_decode else self._prefill_model
+        latency = float(model.predict([features])[0]) * self._latency_scale
+        return max(latency, 0.0)
+
+    def predict_sample_tokens_time(self, total_tokens: int) -> float:
+        """Return the RPC-2 (sample_tokens) duration in seconds.
+
+        ``total_tokens`` is this step's scheduled token count, matching the
+        ``total_tokens`` field written by the GPU-side collection hook.
+        Returns 0.0 when the compensation is not configured.

+        applying it to a hypothetical decode-only deployment extrapolates the
+        token-independent floor beyond its measured domain.
+        """

+            return 0.0
+
+        tt = float(total_tokens)
+        latency = self.sample_tokens_base_s + self.sample_tokens_lo_s_per_token * tt
+        if tt > self.sample_tokens_breakpoint_tokens:
+            latency += (
+                self.sample_tokens_hi_s_per_token - self.sample_tokens_lo_s_per_token
+            ) * (tt - self.sample_tokens_breakpoint_tokens)
+        return max(latency, 0.0)

+"""Oracle lookup predictor — replays real GPU iter_latency from a pre-built table.
+
+Replay is a diagnostic predictor for separating latency-prediction error from
+scheduler, cache, and simulator behavior. A replay table maps a JSON-encoded,
+sorted list of ``[extend_input_length, prefix_length]`` pairs to measured
+forward and sample_tokens latencies in seconds.
+
+Example simulator configuration:
+    "predictor": {
+        "name": "replay",
+        "database_path": "/path/to/replay_table.json",
+        "miss_strategy": "knn",       # "zero" (legacy) or "knn" (interpolated)
+        "miss_knn_k": 3,              # KNN k for "knn" strategy
+        "miss_fallback_seconds": 0.0  # used only when strategy=="zero"
+    }
+
+Build the table from collector exports with
+``ReplayTimePredictor.build_table_from_schedule_batch``.
+"""
+
+import gzip
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import typing
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.types import SchedulerConfig
+from vllm_simulator.spec.accelerator import AcceleratorInfo
+from vllm_simulator.time_predictor.base import InferTimePredictor, ScheduleBatch
+from vllm_simulator.utils import get_logger
+
+if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import ModelConfig
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+def _encode_key(pairs) -> str:
+    """Canonical lookup key: JSON of the sorted [extend, past] pairs."""
+    return json.dumps(sorted(pairs))
+
+
+def _decode_key(key: str):
+    """Parse a sorted-tuple lookup key back to list of (extend, past) pairs."""
+    return [tuple(pair) for pair in json.loads(key)]
+
+
+def _shape_feat(extends, pasts):
+    """3-D feature for KNN: (batch_size, sum_extend, sum_past).
+
+    Low-dim and aligned with the dominant latency drivers; avoids the curse of
+    dimensionality on the typically small (~1-3K) entries per replay table.
+    """
+    return (len(extends), sum(extends), sum(pasts))
+
+
+class ReplayTimePredictor(InferTimePredictor):
+    """Oracle lookup predictor: returns real GPU iter_latency for matching batch compositions.
+
+    Compositions are matched exactly by sorted (extend_len, past_kv_len) tuples.
+    On lookup miss the behavior is controlled by `miss_strategy`:
+
+      - "zero" (default, legacy): returns `miss_fallback_seconds` (default 0.0).
+        Use for "is the gap NOT from the predictor?" diagnostic. Only meaningful
+        when miss rate is small AND you accept the bias of dropping miss work.
+
+      - "knn": KNN-interpolated latency from the k batches in the table with
+        the closest (batch_size, sum_extend, sum_past) shape (per-dim z-scored
+        Euclidean distance). Use when miss rate matters or you want a logically
+        complete oracle. Typical k=3.
+
+    For workloads where sim batch composition diverges from real (e.g., bursty
+    max-tps), the miss rate can be high; prefer "knn" there.
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def build_table_from_schedule_batch(
+        jsonl_paths: str | list[str],
+        output_path: str | None = None,
+    ) -> dict:
+        """Build a replay lookup table from collector schedule_batch export(s).
+
+        Each input line is one scheduled engine step from a
+        ``{rank}.schedule_batch.jsonl[.gz]`` collector export; its
+        ``requests`` field holds ``(req_id, extend_input_len, past_kv_len,
+        output_len)`` tuples. Steps with the same sorted (extend, past)
+        composition are collapsed by averaging ``iter_latency`` and
+        ``sample_tokens_latency`` separately.
+
+        Args:
+            jsonl_paths: One schedule_batch JSONL path, or several to merge
+                (e.g. multiple rounds/ranks). ``.gz`` is auto-detected.
+            output_path: If set, dump the table JSON here; use it as the
+                predictor's ``database_path``.
+
+        Returns:
+            Replay table mapping ``json.dumps(sorted [[extend, past], ...])``
+            to mean forward and sample_tokens latencies in seconds.
+        """
+        if isinstance(jsonl_paths, str):
+            jsonl_paths = [jsonl_paths]
+        forward_sums: dict[str, float] = {}
+        sample_sums: dict[str, float] = {}
+        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
+        n_rows = 0
+        for path in jsonl_paths:
+            opener = gzip.open if path.endswith(".gz") else open
+            with opener(path, "rt") as f:
+                for line in f:
+                    line = line.strip()
+                    if not line:
+                        continue
+                    row = json.loads(line)
+                    requests = row.get("requests") or []
+                    if not requests:
+                        continue
+                    key = _encode_key([r[1], r[2]] for r in requests)
+                    forward = float(row["iter_latency"])
+                    sample = float(row.get("sample_tokens_latency", 0.0))
+                    if not all(
+                        math.isfinite(value) and value >= 0
+                        for value in (forward, sample)
+                    ):
+                        raise ValueError(f"Invalid replay latency in {path}: {row}")
+                    forward_sums[key] = forward_sums.get(key, 0.0) + forward
+                    sample_sums[key] = sample_sums.get(key, 0.0) + sample
+                    counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
+                    n_rows += 1
+        table = {
+            key: {
+                "iter_latency": forward_sums[key] / counts[key],
+                "sample_tokens_latency": sample_sums[key] / counts[key],
+            }
+            for key in forward_sums
+        }
+        if not table:
+            raise ValueError("Cannot build a replay table without scheduled steps")
+        logger.info(
+            "Built replay table from %d schedule_batch steps (%s): "
+            "%d unique compositions, %d duplicates averaged",
+            n_rows,
+            ", ".join(jsonl_paths),
+            len(table),
+            n_rows - len(table),
+        )
+        if output_path:
+            with open(output_path, "w") as f:
+                json.dump(table, f)
+            logger.info("Replay table written to %s", output_path)
+        return table
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        model: "ModelConfig",
+        hw: AcceleratorInfo,
+        config: SchedulerConfig,
+        database_path: str,
+        miss_fallback_seconds: float = 0.0,
+        miss_strategy: str = "zero",
+        miss_knn_k: int = 3,
+        **kwargs,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(model, hw, config)
+        if not database_path or not os.path.exists(database_path):
+            raise FileNotFoundError(
+                f"ReplayTimePredictor database_path not found: {database_path}"
+            )
+        with open(database_path) as f:
+            raw_table = json.load(f)
+        if not raw_table:
+            raise ValueError("Replay table must not be empty")
+        self._table = {}
+        legacy_entries = 0
+        for key, value in raw_table.items():
+            if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
+                forward, sample = float(value), 0.0
+                legacy_entries += 1
+            elif isinstance(value, dict):
+                forward = float(value["iter_latency"])
+                sample = float(value.get("sample_tokens_latency", 0.0))
+            else:
+                raise ValueError(f"Invalid replay table entry for {key}: {value!r}")
+            if not all(
+                math.isfinite(latency) and latency >= 0
+                for latency in (forward, sample)
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(f"Invalid replay latency for {key}: {value!r}")
+            self._table[key] = (forward, sample)
+        if legacy_entries:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Loaded %d legacy replay entries without sample_tokens latency",
+                legacy_entries,
+            )
+        if miss_strategy not in ("zero", "knn"):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"miss_strategy must be 'zero' or 'knn', got {miss_strategy!r}"
+            )
+        self._miss_strategy = miss_strategy
+        self._miss_fallback = float(miss_fallback_seconds)
+        if not math.isfinite(self._miss_fallback) or self._miss_fallback < 0:
+            raise ValueError("miss_fallback_seconds must be finite and non-negative")
+        self._miss_knn_k = int(miss_knn_k)
+        if self._miss_knn_k < 1:
+            raise ValueError("miss_knn_k must be at least 1")
+
+        if self._miss_strategy == "knn":
+            self._prep_knn_index()
+            logger.info(
+                "ReplayTimePredictor loaded %d unique compositions from %s "
+                "(miss_strategy=knn, k=%d)",
+                len(self._table),
+                database_path,
+                self._miss_knn_k,
+            )
+        else:
+            self._knn_feats = None
+            logger.info(
+                "ReplayTimePredictor loaded %d unique compositions from %s "
+                "(miss_strategy=zero, fallback=%.4fs)",
+                len(self._table),
+                database_path,
+                self._miss_fallback,
+            )
+
+    def _prep_knn_index(self):
+        """Build per-feature mean/std + cached (feat, lat) arrays for KNN fallback.
+
+        Uses plain Python (no numpy / sklearn dependency from the predictor side)
+        — table size is ~1K-3K so this is fine. Distance is z-scored Euclidean
+        across (batch_size, sum_extend, sum_past).
+        """
+        feats = []
+        lats = []
+        for key, latencies in self._table.items():
+            extends_pasts = _decode_key(key)
+            extends = [e for e, _ in extends_pasts]
+            pasts = [p for _, p in extends_pasts]
+            feats.append(_shape_feat(extends, pasts))
+            lats.append(latencies)
+        n = len(feats)
+        # per-dim mean/std for z-scoring
+        means = [sum(f[d] for f in feats) / n for d in range(3)]
+        var = [sum((f[d] - means[d]) ** 2 for f in feats) / n for d in range(3)]
+        stds = [math.sqrt(v) if v > 1e-12 else 1.0 for v in var]
+        self._knn_feats = feats
+        self._knn_lats = lats
+        self._knn_mean = means
+        self._knn_std = stds
+
+    def _knn_predict(self, query_feat):
+        """k nearest neighbors over z-scored 3-D shape feature, simple mean."""
+        qz = tuple(
+            (query_feat[d] - self._knn_mean[d]) / self._knn_std[d] for d in range(3)
+        )
+        # compute squared distance to every table entry; pick smallest k
+        # n ≤ ~3K so O(n) per query is fine; sim only calls on misses
+        dists = []
+        for i, f in enumerate(self._knn_feats):
+            fz = (
+                (f[0] - self._knn_mean[0]) / self._knn_std[0],
+                (f[1] - self._knn_mean[1]) / self._knn_std[1],
+                (f[2] - self._knn_mean[2]) / self._knn_std[2],
+            )
+            d2 = (fz[0] - qz[0]) ** 2 + (fz[1] - qz[1]) ** 2 + (fz[2] - qz[2]) ** 2
+            dists.append((d2, i))
+        dists.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
+        k = min(self._miss_knn_k, len(dists))
+        neighbors = [self._knn_lats[i] for _, i in dists[:k]]
+        return tuple(
+            sum(latencies[component] for latencies in neighbors) / k
+            for component in range(2)
+        )
+
+    def predict_step_time(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> tuple[float, float]:
+        if batch.is_empty():
+            return 0.0, 0.0
+        extends = [req.extend_length for req in batch.reqs]
+        pasts = [req.past_kv_length for req in batch.reqs]
+        key = _encode_key([req.extend_length, req.past_kv_length] for req in batch.reqs)
+        latencies = self._table.get(key)
+        if latencies is None:
+            if self._miss_strategy == "knn":
+                return self._knn_predict(_shape_feat(extends, pasts))
+            return self._miss_fallback, 0.0
+        return latencies
+
+    def predict_infer_time(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> float:
+        return self.predict_step_time(batch)[0]

+
+1. Creates VLLMWorker + MultiInstanceBenchmarkRunner
+2. Builds random dataset aligned to block_size
+3. Validates completions, throughput, and created_time
+4. Tests L1 (device) prefix cache hit (>95%)
+5. Tests L2 (host/CPU) cache hit via native kv_offloading (>95%)
+"""
+
+import os
+import random
+from copy import deepcopy
+
+import numpy as np
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark import (
+    BenchmarkConfig,
+    MultiInstanceBenchmarkRunner,
+    from_sample_requests,
+)
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.vllm_worker import VLLMWorker, EngineArgs
+
+# After vllm_worker: its import installs the hooks vLLM must see first.
+from vllm.benchmarks.datasets import RandomDataset  # noqa: E402
+
+os.environ["VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH"] = (
+    os.path.dirname(__file__) + "/assets/config_vllm.json"
+)
+# os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = ""
+
+
+def check_prefix_cache_and_offload(engine_args: dict, prefix_blocks: int = 4):
+    """Check completions, L1 (device) prefix-cache hit, L2 (CPU offload) hit
+    after eviction, and flush for one model.
+
+    Prompts span ``prefix_blocks`` full blocks plus one token.
+    """
+    random.seed(0)
+    np.random.seed(0)
+
+    worker = VLLMWorker(engine_args=EngineArgs(**engine_args))
+    runner = MultiInstanceBenchmarkRunner(workers=[worker])
+
+    # Prefix-cache granularity.  The engine may enlarge the requested size
+    # (backend preference, hybrid alignment) and reports the smallest KV
+    # group's size, which compressed caches (DeepSeek-V4) shrink below it.
+    effective_block_size = max(
+        engine_args["block_size"] or 0,
+        worker._llm.vllm_config.cache_config.block_size,
+    )
+    max_model_len = engine_args.get("max_model_len", 2048)
+    # Prefix caching requires at least 2 full blocks AND prompts must fit in max_model_len
+    min_required_input = effective_block_size * prefix_blocks + 1
+    can_test_prefix_cache = (effective_block_size < max_model_len) and (min_required_input <= max_model_len)
+
+    # Benchmark settings
+    benchmark_config = BenchmarkConfig(request_rate=10, ignore_request_timestamp=True)
+
+    # Build random requests aligned to effective block_size
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
+        engine_args["model"], trust_remote_code=engine_args["trust_remote_code"]
+    )
+
+    if not can_test_prefix_cache:
+        # Hybrid model with huge block_size: just test basic completions
+        print(f"[SKIP] Prefix cache tests: effective block_size={effective_block_size} >= max_model_len={max_model_len}")
+        requests = from_sample_requests(RandomDataset().sample(
+            tokenizer=tokenizer, num_requests=4, input_len=24, output_len=1,
+        ))
+        metrics = runner.benchmark(benchmark_config, requests=requests)
+        assert metrics["completed"] == len(requests)
+        runner.shutdown()
+        return
+
+    # Ensure prompts span enough full blocks for high cache ratio
+    min_input = effective_block_size * prefix_blocks + 1
+    # Calculate how many prompts needed to evict all cached blocks
+    blocks_per_prompt = min_input // effective_block_size
+    num_gpu_blocks = engine_args.get("num_gpu_blocks_override", 100)
+    num_cached = 8
+    # Need enough eviction prompts to overflow the cache
+    evict_prompts_needed = (num_gpu_blocks // blocks_per_prompt) + 1
+    num_prompts = num_cached + 2 + evict_prompts_needed  # cached + gap + eviction
+    requests = from_sample_requests(RandomDataset().sample(
+        tokenizer=tokenizer,
+        num_requests=num_prompts,
+        input_len=min_input,
+        output_len=1,
+    ))
+
+    # Split requests for cache tests
+    cached_reqs = requests[:num_cached]
+    evict_l1_reqs = requests[num_cached + 2:]
+
+    # First run: warm up cache (populates both L1 GPU and L2 CPU)
+    metrics = runner.benchmark(benchmark_config, requests=cached_reqs)
+    assert metrics["completed"] == len(cached_reqs)
+
+    request_stats = runner.get_request_stats()
+    for idx, req in enumerate(request_stats):
+        assert (
+            idx == 0 or req["created_time"] != 0
+        ), "created_time should not be zero when request_rate=10"
+
+    assert metrics["prompt_tokens_cached_ratio"] == 0
+
+    # Second run: hit device cache (L1)
+    metrics = runner.benchmark(benchmark_config, requests=cached_reqs)
+    local_hit = metrics["prompt_tokens_local_cache_hit_ratio"]
+    assert local_hit > 0.95, (
+        f"Expected local cache hit ratio > 0.95, got {local_hit}"
+    )
+
+    # Evict from device cache by filling GPU with other requests
+    _ = runner.benchmark(benchmark_config, requests=evict_l1_reqs)
+
+    # Third run: should hit host (L2 CPU) cache
+    metrics = runner.benchmark(benchmark_config, requests=cached_reqs)
+    ext_hit = metrics["prompt_tokens_external_kv_transfer_ratio"]
+    assert ext_hit > 0.95, (
+        f"Expected external KV transfer ratio > 0.95, got {ext_hit}"
+    )
+
+    # Fourth run: flush_cache clears both device and host caches
+    runner.flush_cache()
+    metrics = runner.benchmark(benchmark_config, requests=cached_reqs)
+    assert metrics["prompt_tokens_cached_ratio"] == 0, (
+        f"Expected no cache hit after flush, got {metrics['prompt_tokens_cached_ratio']}"
+    )
+
+    runner.shutdown()
+
+
+def test_prefix_cache_and_offload():
+    model_engine_args_list = [
+        {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B"},  # MHA
+        {
+            "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B",  # Hybrid (full_attention + linear_attention)
+            # Blocks are aligned to 800 tokens so the attention page matches
+            # the ~3.2MB/layer mamba state page; each KV block costs ~210MB.
+            # Size the host pool so the eviction round (~204 blocks) cannot
+            # evict the cached prompts (~32 blocks): 48 GiB / 210MB ≈ 245

+            "block_size": 256,

+        "kv_offloading_size": 4.0,

+"""
+Test vLLM server-mode simulation.
+
+1. Spawns vLLM simulation server (launch_server.py) as subprocess
+2. Sends requests via OpenAI-compatible /v1/completions API
+3. Validates that requests complete and timing is reasonable
+
+Two modes are covered:
+- BLOCKING: raw requests against the server, engine sleeps the predicted
+  GPU span per step (test_vllm_serving_blocking).
+- NON_BLOCKING: the hijacked `vllm bench serve` client
+  (vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving) replays the traffic logically
+  through simulation.created_time, and the benchmark result is substituted
+  with the simulation metrics computed from the server's per-request stats
+  (test_vllm_serving_non_blocking).
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+
+import requests
+
+os.environ["VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH"] = (
+    os.path.dirname(__file__) + "/assets/config_vllm.json"
+)
+
+MODEL_PATH = "Qwen/Qwen3-8B"
+SERVER_PORT = 18100
+
+
+class VLLMServingRunner:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        model: str,
+        port: int = SERVER_PORT,
+        env_overrides: dict | None = None,
+        **extra_args,
+    ):
+        cmd = [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server",
+            "--model",
+            model,
+            "--port",
+            str(port),
+            "--dtype",
+            "float16",
+            "--load-format",
+            "dummy",
+            "--enforce-eager",
+            "--block-size",
+            "16",
+            "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+            "0.9",
+            "--max-model-len",
+            "8192",
+            "--num-gpu-blocks-override",
+            "1000000",
+        ]
+        for k, v in extra_args.items():
+            flag = "--" + k.replace("_", "-")
+            if v is True:
+                cmd.append(flag)
+            elif v is False:
+                pass
+            else:
+                cmd.extend([flag, str(v)])
+
+        env = os.environ.copy()
+        if env_overrides:
+            env.update(env_overrides)
+        self.port = port
+        self.base_url = f"http://localhost:{port}"
+        self.server_proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, env=env, preexec_fn=os.setsid)
+
+        # Wait for server to be ready
+        dur = 0
+        while dur < 120:
+            try:
+                r = requests.get(f"{self.base_url}/health")
+                if r.status_code == 200:
+                    return
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+            time.sleep(1)
+            dur += 1
+        self.shutdown()
+        raise RuntimeError("Failed to start vLLM simulation server.")
+
+    def completions(self, prompt: str, max_tokens: int = 10) -> dict:
+        """Send a single completion request."""
+        resp = requests.post(
+            f"{self.base_url}/v1/completions",
+            json={
+                "model": MODEL_PATH,
+                "prompt": prompt,
+                "max_tokens": max_tokens,
+                "ignore_eos": True,
+            },
+            timeout=60,
+        )
+        resp.raise_for_status()
+        return resp.json()
+
+    def shutdown(self):
+        if not self.server_proc or self.server_proc.poll() is not None:
+            return
+        os.killpg(self.server_proc.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
+        try:
+            self.server_proc.wait(timeout=10)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            os.killpg(self.server_proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+            self.server_proc.wait()
+        self.server_proc = None
+

+def test_vllm_serving_blocking():
+    """Test vLLM server with BLOCKING mode simulation."""
+    # Scoped to the server process: a module-level os.environ write would
+    # leak into in-process engines of other test modules in the same session.
+    runner = VLLMServingRunner(
+        model=MODEL_PATH, env_overrides={"VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE": "BLOCKING"}
+    )
+
+    try:
+        # Send a few requests sequentially
+        results = []
+        for i in range(3):
+            t0 = time.time()
+            result = runner.completions(prompt=f"Hello world {i}", max_tokens=5)
+            elapsed = time.time() - t0
+            results.append((result, elapsed))
+
+        # Validate responses
+        for i, (result, elapsed) in enumerate(results):
+            assert "choices" in result, f"Request {i}: no choices in response"
+            assert len(result["choices"]) > 0, f"Request {i}: empty choices"
+            text = result["choices"][0]["text"]
+            assert len(text) > 0, f"Request {i}: empty text output"
+            # In BLOCKING mode, each request should take some time due to time.sleep
+            # With AISimulate predictor, each token takes real inference time
+            print(
+                f"  Request {i}: output_tokens={result['usage']['completion_tokens']}, "
+                f"elapsed={elapsed:.3f}s"
+            )
+
+        print("\n[PASS] test_vllm_serving_blocking passed!")
+    finally:
+        runner.shutdown()
+
+
+def test_vllm_serving_non_blocking():
+    """NON_BLOCKING-mode serving driven by the hijacked `vllm bench serve` client.
+
+    The client (vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving) does not pace
+    requests in real time; each request carries simulation.created_time and
+    the server replays the traffic against its virtual clock. The client then
+    computes metrics from stats returned with each non-streaming completion
+    or chat response, with no separate stats endpoint.
+    """
+    num_prompts = 8
+    request_rate = 10
+    result_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="sim_non_blocking_result_")
+
+    runner = VLLMServingRunner(
+        model=MODEL_PATH,
+        port=SERVER_PORT + 1,
+        env_overrides={"VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE": "NON_BLOCKING"},
+    )
+
+    try:
+        for backend in ("openai", "openai-chat"):
+            filename = f"bench_{backend}.json"
+            cmd = [
+                sys.executable,
+                "-m",
+                "vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving",
+                "--backend",
+                backend,
+                "--endpoint",
+                (
+                    "/v1/chat/completions"
+                    if backend == "openai-chat"
+                    else "/v1/completions"
+                ),
+                "--base-url",
+                runner.base_url,
+                "--model",
+                MODEL_PATH,
+                "--dataset-name",
+                "random",
+                "--num-prompts",
+                str(num_prompts),
+                "--random-input-len",
+                "64",
+                "--random-output-len",
+                "8",
+                "--request-rate",
+                str(request_rate),
+                "--seed",
+                "0",
+                "--percentile-metrics",
+                "ttft,tpot,itl,e2el",
+                "--metric-percentiles",
+                "50,75,99",
+                "--num-warmups",
+                "2",
+                "--ready-check-timeout-sec",
+                "60",
+                "--ignore-eos",
+                "--save-result",
+                "--save-detailed",
+                "--result-filename",
+                filename,
+                "--result-dir",
+                result_dir,
+                "--disable-tqdm",
+            ]
+            if backend == "openai-chat":
+                cmd.extend(["--goodput", "ttft:10000", "tpot:10000", "e2el:10000"])
+            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
+            print(proc.stdout)
+            print(proc.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
+            assert proc.returncode == 0, f"{backend} failed:\n{proc.stderr}"
+            assert " Simulation Metrics " in proc.stdout
+            with open(os.path.join(result_dir, filename)) as f:
+                result = json.load(f)
+
+            # The readiness check and warmups must not count toward results.
+            assert result["completed"] == result["num_requests"] == num_prompts
+            assert result["total_output_tokens"] == num_prompts * 8
+            assert result["duration"] > 0
+            assert result["output_throughput"] > 0
+            assert result["mean_ttft_ms"] > 0
+            assert result["mean_e2el_ms"] > 0
+            assert result["p75_ttft_ms"] >= result["p50_ttft_ms"]
+            assert "prompt_tokens_local_cache_hit_ratio" in result
+            if backend == "openai-chat":
+                assert (
+                    abs(result["request_goodput"] - result["request_throughput"]) < 1e-6
+                )
+            else:
+                assert result["request_goodput"] is None
+            assert len(result["ttfts"]) == num_prompts
+            assert (
+                abs(sum(result["ttfts"]) / num_prompts * 1000 - result["mean_ttft_ms"])
+                < 1e-6
+            )
+
+        # The previous round reset the virtual clock, so this non-streaming
+        # request is replayed from its own created_time.
+        created_time = 0.5
+        resp = requests.post(
+            f"{runner.base_url}/v1/completions",
+            json={
+                "model": MODEL_PATH,
+                "prompt": "Hello world",
+                "max_tokens": 4,
+                "ignore_eos": True,
+                "vllm_xargs": {
+                    "simulation": json.dumps(
+                        {"created_time": created_time, "total_request": 1}
+                    ),
+                },
+            },
+            timeout=60,
+        )
+        resp.raise_for_status()
+        stats = resp.json()["kv_transfer_params"]["simulation"]
+        assert stats["created_time"] == created_time
+        assert len(stats["gen_token_latencies"]) == 4
+        assert stats["last_event_time"] > created_time
+
+        print("\n[PASS] test_vllm_serving_non_blocking passed!")
+    finally:
+        runner.shutdown()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    test_vllm_serving_blocking()
+    test_vllm_serving_non_blocking()
